_comment: Registry of upstream data sources for the OurHike pipeline. Generated/updated by discover_sources.py - re-run that script rather than hand-editing urls here. A source discovery cannot see, because it is not an ArcGIS layer behind the Experience Builder app, is registered by hand and marked with a `kind`: discover_sources.py keeps entries it did not rediscover verbatim, so a hand-written entry survives a re-run. lib/source_registry.py is what reads `kind`, and an entry without one is an ArcGIS feature layer.

photo_licence._comment: The basis on which the Photo1..Photo10 images on the ATC facilities layers may be mirrored and served, recorded rather than assumed - CONTRIBUTING.md, 'A note on data and licences'. This is NOT a Creative Commons grant and must not be rendered as one: ATC holds the copyright, and what is recorded here is the permission to use them, not a licence to sublicense them onward. A club inheriting this project needs to re-confirm it in its own name rather than relying on this line.
photo_licence.author: Appalachian Trail Conservancy
photo_licence.basis: Maintainer authorisation, on the basis of Appalachian Trail Conservancy affiliation
photo_licence.open_question: https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/98 - ATC's redistribution and attribution terms are unresolved in general, and settling them should replace this line with the agreed terms.

atc_licence._comment: The basis on which DATA the Appalachian Trail Conservancy publishes on its own ArcGIS org and services may be reused - photo_licence's sibling, extended from the photos to the data layers by the maintainer's declaration of 2026-08-13 ('anything from the ATC is reusable', restated specifically for the FarOut-measured CSI water distances - #688). Scope, stated tightly: facts ATC itself publishes (half-mile points, the Campsite_Sustainability_Index water distances build_water_distance.py takes, whatever future ATC-org layer a change deliberately adopts). It does NOT cover documents the maintaining clubs publish (per-entry licence fields govern those, e.g. gatc_water_sources below), does NOT override editorial holdbacks that are about safety or partnership rather than licensing (CSI's user-created campsites stay unpublished - SOURCE_SURVEY.md §3b), and is not a grant to sublicense ATC's work onward.
atc_licence.author: Appalachian Trail Conservancy
atc_licence.basis: Maintainer authorisation, on the basis of Appalachian Trail Conservancy affiliation
atc_licence.open_question: ATC's own written terms remain the ideal - SOURCE_SURVEY.md §10's combined ask (capacity, Helene status, CSI, half-mile points) is now a confirmation rather than a blocker, and its answer should replace this line, the same way photo_licence's open question reads.

sources.title: A.T. Trail Updates
sources.licence: Facts and a link only, and NOT a grant to mirror ATC's prose. What is published is the mile range, category, states, headline and ATC's own last-updated date, with a link back to their page - facts about the trail, which is a different thing from the paragraphs ATC wrote about them. #458 asked ATC directly what may be republished and was closed without asking, on the maintainer's judgement as an ATC trail volunteer; that decision settles the conservative version and not the broader one, so the body text stays on ATC's own page. A club inheriting this project needs to confirm this in its own name rather than relying on this line - the same footing as `photo_licence` above and the general question in https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/98.

freshness.notes: The RSS feed, used as a change signal and NOT as the content. Measured 2026-08-24: it held 3 items while the listing held 89 across ten paginated pages, so building the artifact from it would silently drop the most consequential closure (features/ATC_TRAIL_UPDATES.md, 'what the feed does not carry'). The 2026-08-09 version of this note read '3 items while the page showed 9'; the 9 was page one mistaken for the whole list, which is https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/945. It does carry an ETag that moves when ATC edits, which is all a freshness marker needs - WEAK (`W/"..."`) as measured 2026-08-24, where this note said 'strong' on 2026-08-12; check_freshness.py compares it verbatim and only asks whether it moved, but a weak validator lets the upstream change the bytes without changing the tag. The listing page itself is still not usable as the marker, and now for two reasons. The correction this note carried briefly on 2026-08-24 - 'it no longer 403s a scripted request, it answers 200' - was measured with curl and did not describe the pipeline's own client: re-measured the same day, ATC refuses the literal `python-requests/*` User-Agent with 403 and answers 200 to curl and to a named agent, so the original 2026-08-12 finding was right about check_freshness.py and still is. lib/atc_scrape.py reaches the listing only because it sets a User-Agent naming the project. On top of that, a HEAD on the listing returns neither an ETag nor a Last-Modified, so even an allowed request would give a marker of UNKNOWN forever.

sources.discovered_via: features/ATC_TRAIL_UPDATES.md - read from ATC's public website, not from an ArcGIS service. Registered by hand because discover_sources.py walks the Experience Builder app and this source is not in it.
sources.notes: Not fetched by fetch_all.py and has no data/raw/<key>.geojson - the build input is the reviewed file named in `reviewed_input`, which a human edits and a merged pull request releases (#460). The freshness marker is what tells that human ATC has published something since they last looked.

sources.title: A.T. centerline with elevation (ATC's ATX Ratings, Centerline Current)
sources.return_z_comment: The elevation is the geometry's Z, and f=geojson drops it: asked with f=geojson&returnZ=true this layer answered 2-D coordinates, with f=json&returnZ=true [x, y, z] on every vertex (measured 2026-10-03). So the extract reads it as Esri JSON (lib/arcgis.py's iter_layer_pages, return_z).
sources.licence: NOTHING STATED ON THE ITEM: the ATX Ratings item's licenseInfo, accessInformation and description, and the service's copyrightText, are all empty (read 2026-10-03). It is ATC's own ArcGIS Online organization ('Appalachian Trail Conservancy', urlKey ATConservancy), so atc_licence's maintainer authorisation for 'facts ATC itself publishes' is the basis, and the same caveat travels with it: NOT A LICENCE FROM ATC.
sources.key_comment: `GlobalID`: unique on all 697 rows (the elevation read's own measurement, 2026-10-03, in `notes`), the layer's own id. `id_field` names the object id, which a reload mints again (decision 40). `full_ID` is unique only on the 679 rows with a geometry: OBJECTID 681 to 698 repeat segment 25-01-03 with none, so each keeps its own GlobalID and its row.
sources.elevation_unit_comment: Measured 2026-10-03: 6 vertices on 2 segments (Katahdin, Baxter Peak to Katahdin Stream Campground; and one in northern Virginia) against 3DEP through EPQS. Read as metres the median difference is 1.93 m (largest 11.6 m, on Katahdin's tableland); read as feet it is 401 m. The layer states no vertical unit: its spatial reference carries no vcsWkid. The Baxter Peak end vertex reads 1,600.48 against the summit's published 5,267 ft (1,605 m), Reasoned.
sources.discovered_via: reference/org_coverage.json's AVAILABLE_NOT_LOADED elevation row for this club (coverage audit 2026-10-01), then re-read live on 2026-10-03 for decision 54's wave 1 under lib/user_agent.py's USER_AGENT, robots.txt first: the layer's own metadata, returnCountOnly, an attribute-only read of every row for the key, and a few vertices or points compared with USGS 3DEP through EPQS for the elevation unit.
sources.notes: 697 rows (returnCountOnly), 25 fields, polyline, hasZ and hasM true, maxRecordCount 2,000, served in EPSG:3857, dataLastEditDate 2025-10-01, all measured 2026-10-03. OBJECTID and GlobalID are each unique on all 697. 18 ROWS HAVE NO GEOMETRY: OBJECTID 681 to 698 repeat segment 25-01-03 (OBJECTID 192) attribute for attribute with a null Shape__Length, so the layer holds 679 lines, 4,586,382 m of them, and full_ID is unique on those 679 only. N_end_mileage and S_end_mileage are null on every row. THE LAYER IS EDITABLE BY ANYONE: capabilities read 'Create,Delete,Query,Update,Editing' on a public item, and editorTrackingInfo reads allowAnonymousToUpdate and allowAnonymousToDelete true. That reading is Reasoned from the metadata and was not tested, since testing it means writing to ATC's layer; it means a Z value here can change without ATC changing it. Layers 1, 5 and 10 of the same service and Map/FeatureServer/0 are copies (atc/elevation.py's SAME_AS notes).
sources.reaches_hikers_comment: Registered for decision 54 (load every dataset the clubs publish), not shipped: no model reads this table yet. Phase C flips this to true when its generated base model and the elevation union read it. Until then false, because an elevation figure that reached a phone before anyone checked it against the 3DEP profile would be a display outrunning its source (CLAUDE.md).

sources.title: GATC Water Sources (approach trail + Georgia A.T.)
sources.licence: Unstated - a free public download from GATC's own site, fetched for REVIEW AND CROSS-CHECKS ONLY. Nothing from this source reaches a published artifact until GATC answers a redistribution ask (CONTRIBUTING.md, 'A note on data and licences'; the ask is the same shape as https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/98 records for opentrail.org). WATER_SOURCES.md §4 sizes this document as 'a pilot-state candidate after an email' and notes its embedded title is 'GATC Water Update July 2020.xlsx', so the 2026-03 file may re-export older data - a second reason the ask precedes any publication.
sources.discovered_via: SOURCE_SURVEY.md §5's club sweep (the 'water-sources PDF (2026-03-02)' row); fetched and parsed live 2026-08-13 (#669). Registered by hand - discover_sources.py walks the Experience Builder app and this source is not in it.
sources.notes: Fetched by fetch_club_pdfs.py to data/raw/club_pdfs/<key>.pdf (never by fetch_all.py), parsed by lib/club_pdfs.py to <key>.json beside it: 65 rows (4 approach trail + 61 A.T., measured on the live PDF 2026-08-13, agreeing with WATER_SOURCES.md §4's count) of GATC mile point + entry text. The PDF's text layer stores each printed row as one string, so the 'Source Name' and 'Distance Off AT' columns arrive fused and are kept that way rather than split by guesswork - lib/club_pdfs.py's docstring holds the measurement.

sources.licence: Facts and a link only (decision 53, features/ORG_NOTICES.md §7), on the maintainer's 2026-10-03 decision to publish every club's notices that way; NOT a grant from the Georgia Appalachian Trail Club. The terms read are quoted in `terms`; none of them bears on reading or on automated collection. The bear-canister rule it carries is the Forest Service's order; GATC republishes it.
sources.terms: None found: no terms page found on georgia-atclub.org (decision 53 inventory, batch 4, 2026-10-03).
sources.person_fields_comment: What the source carries that names or reaches a person, none of which lands: the reader keeps only the fields it names (extract/_notices.py's FEED_COLUMNS and PAGE_COLUMNS, extract/_kinds.py's WP_DROPPED), so these never reach the raw store (pipeline/ELT.md, 'Who may publish', rule 8; decision 59).

freshness.notes: No validator trusted: every run reads the source (one request) and is FRESH only when the rows that would land hash as the last committed load did (extract/_notices.py's change check).

sources.discovered_via: pipeline/ELT.md decision 53 phase A inventory, batch 4, measured 2026-10-03; registered in phase B (pages, feeds and WordPress).
sources.notes: The `alerts` custom post type's feed, the only machine-readable route to it (the type is absent from /wp-json/wp/v2/types). Its weak ETag and Last-Modified are identical on /feed/ and /alerts/feed/, a site-wide cache stamp, so the check is the read. georgia-atclub.org asks `Crawl-delay: 10`. Read live at 2026-10-03T22:07:56Z under lib/user_agent.py's agent, robots.txt allows the path for our agent, Crawl-delay 10: HTTP 200, 3,307 bytes, ETag W/"51bf3e3b1ad6118c2729a84ad48ab8b8" and Last-Modified Sat, 03 Oct 2026 20:11:26 GMT. Through FeedNotices that answer lands 2 rows, one an item, `item_id` taken from the guid on 2 and distinct on 2 of 2: the key. The proof is the item count of the same answer (`feed_items`), so an empty feed is a proven zero, and every row carries `listing = 'window'`.
sources.reaches_hikers_comment: Held, decision 63's hold (2026-10-04): GATC's organization row says nothing of theirs reaches a hiker until GATC answers a redistribution ask (org:gatc; tests/test_export_sources.py holds that no Georgia steward is named), and no decision records that decision 55's facts and a link reach past it. Settled by the maintainer saying whether it does, or by GATC's answer.

sources.title: OSM water point sources (fourteen A.T. states)
sources.licence: ODbL 1.0 - attribution and share-alike, the terms the self-built basemap already complies with; the client's credits screen names OpenStreetMap and each published water point's description carries 'Mapped by OpenStreetMap contributors'. This is the openly licensed half of #529's water answer - no ask pending, unlike the ATC and club rows above.
sources.discovered_via: WATER_SOURCES.md's census for #529 (spike_osm_water_census.py) measured OSM point sources within 250 m of 26% of shelters trail-wide and 40% in the south, against 8% for the shipped supply. Registered by hand - discover_sources.py walks the Experience Builder app and this source is not in it.
sources.notes: Fetched by fetch_osm_water.py to data/raw/osm_water.geojson (never by fetch_all.py): nodes tagged natural=spring, amenity=drinking_water, man_made=water_tap or man_made=water_well across the fourteen Geofabrik state extracts export_basemap.py already downloads - 7,574 nodes on the first full scan (2026-08-13). No freshness entry on purpose: Geofabrik republishes the extracts daily, so a changed-marker would always say yes (export_basemap.py's docstring holds the reasoning; the fetch is skip-if-present with --refetch). export_poi.py folds these into poi_type water at low confidence, dropping each point within 25 m of an opentrail water point as the same node arriving twice.

sources.title: 3D Hydrography Program (3DHP)
sources.licence: Public domain, as a work of the United States government — the whole USGS hydrography column (WATER_SOURCES.md §5). Attribution is courtesy rather than obligation, and the client's credits screen already names USGS for NHD.

freshness.notes: The distinct `workunitid` values 3DHP's flowline layer returns for boxes on the trail. `NHD` is 3DHP saying, in its own field, that these lines are the retired dataset republished rather than anything it has surveyed - measured 2026-08-14 at five points spread along the trail from North Carolina (mile 110) to New Hampshire (mile 1,868), every one of them `NHD`. When that stops being the answer, 3DHP has resurveyed the corridor and the migration this pipeline is deliberately not doing becomes worth costing. Changing `recorded` is how a person acknowledges having looked; nothing writes it automatically.

sources.discovered_via: WATER_SOURCES.md §5, following USGS's retirement of the NHD on 2023-10-01. Registered by hand - discover_sources.py walks ATC's Experience Builder app and this is not in it.
sources.notes: Nothing fetches this. It is registered because the pipeline's water derivation (fetch_trail_water.py) reads a dataset USGS no longer maintains, and this is where its replacement will appear. Measured 2026-08-14: for the corridor, 3DHP IS NHD - identical geometry (1,265 flowlines in a box in central Virginia against NHD's 1,265, same vertex count, worst-case separation 0.086 mm) and identical springs (1,796 features, every one within 1 m of an NHD spring) - with the perennial/intermittent FCode collapsed away into an undifferentiated `Channel Line`. Migrating now would trade the only structured seasonality signal the pipeline has for the same geometry, so the entry holds a watch instead of a fetch.

sources.title: USGS Volcano Hazards: volcanoes at an elevated alert level
sources.licence: Public domain, as a work of the United States government (17 U.S.C. 105), the reading usgs_3dhp is registered on. No terms were read for this API, and its host serves no robots.txt (404, the decision 53 inventory, batch 1, 2026-10-03). Facts and a link only (decision 53).

freshness.notes: No ETag and no Last-Modified (inventory, 2026-10-03): one request of about 3 KB every hourly run. A 200 with a JSON list is the answer and its length the count; an empty list is Reasoned to mean nothing is elevated, not observed.

sources.discovered_via: pipeline/ELT.md decision 53's phase A inventory, batch 1 (usgs-tnm), registered in phase B. Lands in _shared/usgs/, beside 3DEP and NHD, as a national service.
sources.notes: 5 volcanoes on 2026-10-03: Gareloi, Shishaldin and Ahyi Seamount YELLOW/ADVISORY, Great Sitkin and Kilauea ORANGE/WATCH. Fields: obs_fullname, obs_abbr, volcano_name, vnum, notice_type_cd, notice_identifier, sent_utc, sent_unixtime, color_code, alert_level, notice_url, notice_data. The key is vnum (unique on 5 of 5): three AVO volcanoes shared one notice_identifier that day, so the notice cannot key the table. No coordinates; vnum is the Smithsonian volcano number. It reaches a hiker only where a drawn trail is near a volcano (the Cascades, Hawaii, Alaska), which is dbt's join to make.
sources.reaches_hikers_comment: Held, decision 63's hold (2026-10-04): no geometry, and its own notes say it reaches a hiker only where a drawn trail is near the volcano, a join no model makes; unplaced, a row would reach every hiker or none. Settled by that join.

sources.title: USGS post-fire debris-flow hazard assessments (locations)
sources.licence: PUBLIC DOMAIN, on 17 U.S.C. 105 and the maintainer's adoption of it for usfs_trails (2026-09-02). A work prepared by an officer or employee of the U.S. Government as part of their official duties is not subject to domestic copyright, so there is nothing here for the agency to grant or withhold - which is why this is `stated_by_org` rather than `maintainer_authorisation`, on usfs_trails' own reasoning.
sources.discovered_via: pipeline/ELT.md decision 53 phase A inventory, batch 1, measured 2026-10-03; registered in phase B (ArcGIS).

sources.notes: 8,823 point features statewide, measured 2026-08-18. The layer's own display name is 'NY State Parks Facilities (Internal)' although the service is public - what that naming implies about the schema's intended audience is unassessed. dataLastEditDate verified live 2026-08-18 (then 2026-08-12). IT CARRIES WATER, measured live 2026-08-27 and answering the question #769 and NYC_SOURCE_SURVEY.md §10(g) left open: `Sub_Asset` has 158 distinct values, among them **136 'Water Spigot' and 15 'Drinking Fountain'** (plus 'Mineral Spring', 'Water Tower' and 'Waterfall', which are not drinking water and must not be read as such). So the evidence bar CLAUDE.md's four ways sets is now live for this layer rather than hypothetical - shipping it is a water change, and needs export_poi.py's confidence and provenance treatment the way `osm_water` got one, not a plain point dump. `Asset` is a coded integer 1-17 whose domain the service does NOT publish, so the type of a facility is only readable through `Sub_Asset`'s free text; that is the join hazard to solve before any of these become waypoints. HOW THAT RESOLVED: the layer ships as of 2026-08-27 (#1097) via export_nearby_poi.py, which reads the type through `Sub_Asset`'s free text as this note said it would have to, and `reaches_hikers` is true for that reason. The water is the one part held back, and the sentence above about the evidence bar is why - see oprhp_water_holdback for the two questions that have to be answered before a spigot becomes a pin. An earlier version of this note ended '`reaches_hikers` stays false because nothing exports this layer'; that was true when written and survived the export being wired, which is the failure it is now recorded against.
sources.public_field_comment: NOT `Public_`, which reads Y on all 8,823 rows and therefore discriminates nothing (measured 2026-08-27). ParksApp is the field that does, 5,822 Y / 3,000 N - but it records what OPRHP's own visitor app SHOWS rather than what exists on the ground, so it SETS CONFIDENCE rather than filtering: dropping its N side would discard every one of OPRHP's 37 lean-tos, none of which are in that app. An N row ships at CONFIDENCE_LOW, which the map draws with a broken rim and the legend's 'Verified?' filter removes. This is the opposite reading from DEC's PUBLICUSE and the difference is measured, not stylistic - see export_nearby_poi.py's docstring and POI_COVERAGE_SURVEY.md §2.
sources.id_field_comment: Declared rather than left to export_nearby_poi.py's `OBJECTID` default, which is what this entry did until now - alone among the six POI layers, every DEC one of which declares it. The default gave the right answer, so nothing was wrong on the ground; what was wrong is that the registry did not RECORD the join, and a reader comparing this entry against DEC's could only conclude the layer had no stable id. It does: the service's own `objectIdField` and `uniqueIdField` both read OBJECTID, verified live 2026-08-28.
sources.name_field_comment: `Name` is populated on 1,631 of 8,823 rows (18%, measured 2026-08-27) and is flagged '(Legacy Field)' in the layer's own alias. The other 82% export with no name and the client renders them 'Unnamed', which is the honest outcome: `Facility` (populated on all 8,823) is the PARK's name, not the feature's, and publishing 'Beaver Island State Park' as the name of a bridge inside it would be a different fact than the one a hiker reads. It goes into the composed description instead - export_nearby_poi.py's compose_description, which is lib/poi_description.py's idea applied to another org's columns.

sources.title: NYNJTC Trail Alerts
sources.licence: See nynjtc_notices_licence below. Registered 2026-08-27 as unsettled and authorised by the maintainer the same day; what ships is the conservative facts-and-a-link split ATC's notices already ship on - title, locality, NYNJTC's own date and a link to their page, never their body text. NYNJTC's own terms remain the ideal and the ask is still open (https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/768).

freshness.notes: The category's RSS feed, used as a change signal and NOT as the content - the same division `atc_trail_updates` uses, and for the same reason: measured 2026-08-27 the feed held 12 items while the API held all 18, so building from it would silently drop six alerts. It is a BETTER marker than ATC's on both counts that matter. The validator is STRONG (`"b04bf0f8..."`, no `W/` prefix) where ATC's is weak, so a change to the bytes cannot leave the tag standing; and a `Last-Modified` is served beside it (Wed, 26 Aug 2026 21:41:57 GMT), giving check_freshness.py a second marker if the first is ever dropped. NYNJTC also does not refuse a scripted request the way ATC's host refuses the literal `python-requests/*` User-Agent - verified 2026-08-27 with urllib's default agent, which answered 200 - so nothing here depends on naming ourselves. fetch_nynjtc_alerts.py names the project anyway, as courtesy rather than necessity.

sources.discovered_via: pipeline/ALERTS_NOTICES_SURVEY.md §5b - the alerts survey #1073 ran across every org whose trails this build draws. Registered by hand: discover_sources.py walks ATC's Experience Builder app and this is a WordPress category, not a layer.
sources.notes: Fetched by fetch_nynjtc_alerts.py to data/raw/nynjtc_alerts.json (never by fetch_all.py, which fetches ArcGIS layers only) and exported by export_nynjtc_alerts.py to conditions/nynjtc_alerts.json, which publish.py uploads. WHAT `reaches_hikers: true` MEANS HERE, stated because this source reached it by a different road from every other one: an exporter reads it and its rows reach a release, which is the field's definition (reaches_hikers_comment). Every row ships in the WEAKEST form the design allows - `place: unplaced`, `obstructs_trail: false`, `review_state: unreviewed` - because reference/notice_places.json does not exist yet and nobody has reviewed NYNJTC's page. So the map draws none of these and the client surfaces them as a list a hiker reads, which is features/ORG_NOTICES.md §3's first-class unplaced state rather than a gap. 18 alerts on 2026-08-27, published 2024-01-11 to 2026-06-16, read from the WordPress REST API - `/wp-json/wp/v2/posts?categories=6` - rather than scraped, which is the whole difference from `atc_trail_updates`: there is no markup to misread, and `per_page`/`modified_after`/`_fields` are query parameters rather than things to reimplement. THE FIND THE SURVEY ITSELF MISSED, corrected in §5b the same day: NYNJTC tags each alert from its own CLOSED taxonomies, so placement is a join against tens of terms rather than a fuzzy match of prose against the 21,805 exported network features. Coverage measured on those 18 - park on 17, trail on 10, region and state on 7 each - and the trail vocabulary is 45 terms, the park vocabulary 125. That last number is why the fetcher pages every list route: `park` answers exactly 100 to a single per_page=100 request, and a vocabulary truncated there would drop placements with no error anywhere. ONE HYGIENE WART, recorded so it is not mistaken for a parser bug: `highlands-trail` is a term in BOTH the trail and park taxonomies (ids 31 and 405), so a join table must key on `taxonomy:slug` and never on the slug alone. features/ORG_NOTICES.md is the delivery design and holds the placement, dedup and voice questions; none of them is settled by this registration.

sources.title: NYNJTC Long Path End-to-End Section Guide (40 section pages)
sources.licence: See nynjtc_guide_licence below. NYNJTC has stated no reuse terms; their site terms claim copyright over its text and maps (Terms & Conditions section 3, read 2026-09-08). This ships on the maintainer's authorisation of 2026-09-08 - 'make reach_hikers:true - I'm assuming my relationship with nynjtc is enough' - the same footing nynjtc_notices_licence records for their alerts, and it covers this guide's FACTS only: a type, a position, a section and mile, an off-trail distance, a short name and the page URL, never the guide's sentence. The maintainer's NYNJTC conversation (https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/768) remains where NYNJTC's own answer belongs.
sources.discovered_via: The maintainer's ask, 2026-09-08 (https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/1288): 'augment the Longpath data from NYNJTC ... extract the POI's from the section guide'. The same forty pages the registered nynjtc_long_path layer links to from its own GuideURL field, so the join between a page and the line it describes is NYNJTC's rather than ours. Registered by hand: discover_sources.py walks ATC's Experience Builder app and this is a WordPress site, not a layer.
sources.notes: Fetched by fetch_nynjtc_long_path_guide.py to data/raw/nynjtc_long_path_guide/ (never by fetch_all.py, which fetches ArcGIS layers only): the index page plus forty section pages, lp-section-1 through lp-section-40, as WordPress serves them, and sections.json beside them - lib/nynjtc_long_path_guide.py's parse of each page into its Distance header and its Parking, Camping and Detailed Trail Description blocks. MEASURED 2026-09-08 on all forty pages: 1,256 mile-marked entries, 153 of them carrying NYNJTC's own coordinates to five decimals (almost all in the Parking blocks), and every page in one skeleton (section 22 adds a Winter Access block). WHAT THE PARSE PLACES, the same day, against the live nynjtc_long_path layer: 271 waypoints after merging the 61 places the guide says more than once - 120 parking, 92 viewpoints, 21 water sources, 17 shelters, 17 campsites, 4 privies. 153 entries sit where NYNJTC's coordinates put them (CONFIDENCE_HIGH); 164 are placed by walking the guide's mile along the section's line (CONFIDENCE_LOW), an estimate whose along-trail error was measured against the entries that carry both a mile and coordinates - median 86 m, p90 476 m - and is carried on each such record as position_error_m 500. 14 entries NYNJTC marks '(unlocated)' are not placed. THE PAGES SERVE NO VALIDATOR: no ETag and no Last-Modified (read 2026-09-08, cache-control public max-age=300), and the body hash is no change signal either - two fetches an hour apart differ in every WordPress gallery's random galleryId - so the fetcher compares the PARSE of each page against its own manifest (content_sha256) and reports which sections' facts moved. There is no freshness block here because check_freshness.py has no marker to watch. Forty-one requests per run, throttled to two a second, naming the project in the User-Agent. The interactive map at nynjtc.org/long-path-interactive-map/ was read the same day and adds nothing point-shaped: its web map (item 5d9da6d5ec74469a96393364f4384609) holds the registered Long Path layer plus the Shawangunk Ridge Trail and West Point seasonal-route line layers ALERTS_NOTICES_SURVEY.md already catalogues. WHAT A RECORD CARRIES, now that it ships (reaches_hikers flipped 2026-09-08 on the maintainer's authorisation, recorded in nynjtc_guide_licence): the type, the position, the section and the guide's mile within it, an off-trail distance where the guide states one, a short name where the entry has one, and the URL of the page - never the guide's sentence, which is NYNJTC's writing (the same split nynjtc_notices_licence draws for their alerts).

sources.title: NYNJTC Hike Finder export (the full 385-hike list)
sources.licence: See nynjtc_hikes_licence below, which this source inherits and does not widen. The permission is the same one #1290 recorded - the maintainer's relay of NYNJTC's, 'we have their permission' (2026-09-08) and 'We can use anything' (2026-09-09) - and the only thing that changed on 2026-09-15 is the ROAD the data arrives by: the maintainer supplied the full list as this export instead of the 20 public pages nynjtc.org serves. WHAT IS GENUINELY NEW HERE IS THE ROUTE. nynjtc.org publishes no line for any hike, which is why #1290's routes had to be constructed and reviewed one at a time; this export publishes a GPX track for 113 of its 385 hikes, and that track is a line the publisher DREW rather than anything this build inferred. It ships as the route, unmodified - its geometry only; see the notes below for why its elevations are not used. The other 272 still publish only a parking pin and a description, and the line a hiker sees for those is OurHike's construction over this build's own trail lines - the card says so, in the word `generated`, and route_hikefinder.py refuses to ship one it cannot stand behind. THE HOST IS NOT NYNJTC. heardimmunity.org is the maintainer's own, so reading it is not reading somebody else's site, and this entry carries no robots or rate question of NYNJTC's; the CONTENT is still NYNJTC's and every condition nynjtc_hikes_licence names - the attribution, the link back, no sublicensing onward - applies to it unchanged.
sources.discovered_via: The maintainer's ask, 2026-09-15 (https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/1427): 'we finally got the full list of hikes from NYNJTC. Can you load all the hikes from here, and stop scraping the website ... About 100 have the route fully planned. Use the route from the .gpx. The other 300 need the route formed.' Registered by hand: discover_sources.py walks ATC's Experience Builder app and this is a PHP export, not a layer.
sources.notes: Fetched by fetch_hikefinder.py to data/raw/hikefinder.json and data/raw/hikefinder_gpx/ (never by fetch_all.py, which fetches ArcGIS layers only), read as HTML: the export publishes no JSON API and no bulk download, so `hikes.php` is the index and `hike.php?id=N` is the record. MEASURED 2026-09-15 against the live export: `hikes.php` prints 'Results (385 hikes found)' and links exactly 385 distinct `hike.php?id=N` pages, ids 1-450 with gaps. All 385 parsed, none refused. EVERY PAGE CARRIES THE SAME TWELVE LABELLED FIELDS - Length, Difficulty, Estimated Time, Route Type, Dogs, Park, Region, Author, GPS Coordinates, Features, Publish Date, Last Updated - and the parse found all twelve present on all 385: a stated length on 385, a difficulty on 385, a route type on 385, a park and a region on 385, a coordinate on 385. Free-text cards around them: a Description on 385, Directions to Trailhead on 383, a Summary on 369, Public Transportation on 81, Last Updated on 306. VOCABULARIES, as published and unmapped: route type is Circuit 321, Lollipop 34, Shuttle 17, Out and back 13; difficulty is SIX levels, not the five nynjtc.org's taxonomy used - Moderate 132, Easy To Moderate 78, Easy 69, Moderate To Strenuous 60, Strenuous 45, Very Strenuous 1. THE FEATURES ARE THE TAGS and the maintainer asked for all of them kept ('especially the tags'): 13 distinct across the corpus - Views 313, Historic feature 148, Waterfall 58, Cliffs 56, Public Transportation 54, Fees 44, Woods 23, Swimming 19, Birding 17, Bikes allowed 17, Wildflowers 9, Horses allowed 6, Accessible 3 - carried as published, in page order, with no mapping onto a vocabulary of this build's own. THE ROUTE SPLIT IS THE POINT OF THIS SOURCE: 113 pages offer `download_gpx.php?id=N`, which answers application/gpx+xml (id 50 returns 943 trkpt, every one carrying ele in metres); those 113 ship the publisher's own track, unmodified and ungraded against this build's lines, because a line the publisher drew outranks a line this pipeline inferred from their prose. THEY ARE DRAWN, NOT RECORDED, and an earlier version of this entry called them a survey - corrected 2026-09-15 (#1451) after the maintainer questioned it. Measured over all 113: 110 carry creator="https://gpx.studio" (a route-drawing tool), 2 of the other 3 are komoot and 1 is GPS Visualizer, only 2 files carry any <time> element at all, and none carries a heart-rate, cadence or speed extension - a recorded track timestamps essentially every point. THE ELEVATIONS ARE A SURFACE SAMPLED ALONG THE LINE, and the corpus is split about how obviously, so it is stated as a split rather than the flatter sentence this entry first carried: 55 of the 113 files have over 90% of their elevation steps on an exact 0.25 m grid (the commonest small steps are precisely 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00 m), which is a raster; the other 53 have under 20% on that grid and step by hundredths of a metre instead, which is an interpolation. Neither half is an altimeter. Per-track median nonzero step 0.75 m (p25 0.53, p75 0.86); largest step in a whole track a median 6.5 m (p25 5.2, p75 8.8); consecutive pairs byte-identical a median 7.4% (p25 2.7%, p75 11.9%). SO THE ELEVATIONS ARE NOT USED: a published hike's climb is priced from this build's own elevation sidecar over the re-walked line, exactly as a generated hike's is, and is absent when the sidecar cannot price it. The other 272 publish one coordinate the page itself labels '(Parking location)' plus a turn-by-turn description, and lib/hike_route_builder.py forms a route from them over trail_graph.json, grading every one and shipping none it cannot stand behind. HOW FAR THE PARKING IS FROM THE TRAIL, measured over all 385 coordinates against the 2026-09-14 graph: 247 within 45.7 m (the phone's own MAX_OFF_NETWORK_M), 312 within 100 m, 328 within 200 m, 345 within 1 km, 31 further than 2 km from any line this build draws, median 22.2 m. BEHIND A SITE PASSWORD SINCE 2026-09-15 (#1468), between a clean fetch at 02:18 and the first failed one at 08:04. hikes.php serves a login form - one `site_password` field posted to the same URL, answered with a PHPSESSID cookie - and every page behind it answers 200 with that login page rather than an error, which is why the listing guard rather than a status code is what catches it. fetch_hikefinder.py signs in once per run from the HIKEFINDER_PASSWORD environment variable, injected on the fetch step of publish-vector-data.yml from a GitHub Actions secret. THE PASSWORD IS NOT IN THIS FILE AND MUST NEVER BE: this registry is exported to hikers as registry.json. A run without the variable fetches as an anonymous reader and, if the export is locked, lands on the listing guard - so a missing secret costs the hikes, never the A.T. data (#1462). NO FRESHNESS BLOCK, and check_freshness.py is deliberately not taught one: measured 2026-09-15 the export serves neither an ETag nor a Last-Modified on hikes.php and publishes no feed, so the fetcher compares each page's own Last Updated field against its previous cache and reports what moved - the shape fetch_nynjtc_long_path_guide.py settled on for pages with no validator. 499 requests on a cold run (one listing, 385 pages, 113 tracks) and 386 on a warm one, throttled to two a second, naming the project in the User-Agent.

sources.notes: 304 polyline segments, measured live 2026-08-25 via returnCountOnly. sources.title: NYS DEC Hiking Trails (statewide, DEC Info Locator)
sources.steward: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation
sources.licence: See dec_licence below. DEC has stated no terms of their own - copyrightText is empty on the service and on this layer, both read live 2026-08-25 - so this ships on the maintainer's authorisation of 2026-08-25, the same footing atc_licence, nynjtc_licence and mohonk_licence already use.
sources.attribution: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation
sources.foot_allowed_comment: WHAT `M` IN THE FOOT COLUMN IS READ AS, because dec_hiking_trails' foot_allowed keeps those 1,236 rows and the reading is ours rather than DEC's. DEC's CORRIDOR USE domain declares five codes with these labels, read off the live field metadata 2026-08-25: Y=YES, N=NO, U=UNDECIDED, M=MAINTAINED, -99=NO JURISDICTION. `M` is read here as 'DEC maintains this corridor for foot travel', which is at least as strong a statement about walkability as Y. @unvalidated - DEC publishes no data dictionary this project has found that defines the code per row, so the reading rests on the domain's own label plus what the rows look like: measured 2026-08-25, 991 of the 1,236 M rows are ASSET 'FOOT TRAIL', 681 carry a trail-marker colour, and the named ones are ordinary hiking trails (Bog Meadow Trail, the Finger Lakes Trail, the North Country Trail, the Long Path). What would settle it: DEC's own documentation of the CORRIDOR USE matrix, or the same conversation open_question above names. What the alternative costs: a foot_allowed of ['Y'] alone drops 23% of the layer DEC itself publishes as hiking trails, including named through-trails - a hiking-only filter deleting hiking trails, which is the wrong way for this to fail.
sources.discovered_via: pipeline/NYC_SOURCE_SURVEY.md §3's verdict - 'register next', written 2026-08-18 from the maintainer's own lead (gisservices.dec.ny.gov/gis/dil/, 'Outdoor Activity') - acted on under #1019, whose scope decision is what made a Catskills source non-optional. Registered by hand: this is an on-prem ArcGIS server rather than an AGOL org, so there is no item to discover and discover_sources.py has nothing to walk.
sources.notes: 5,286 polyline segments (4,931 LineString, 355 MultiLineString), fetched whole and counted 2026-08-25 - against the 5,277 NYC_SOURCE_SURVEY.md §3 read on 2026-08-11, so the layer moves. Fields UNIT/FACILITY/NAME/ASSET/MILES/DESCRIP/PUBLICUSE/UPDATED plus the per-use CORRIDOR USE matrix (FOOT/HORSE/BIKE/XC/SNOWMB/ATV/MOTORV/ADMIN/ACCESSIBLE/MAPPWD) and MARKER, which DEC aliases 'Trail Marker Color' and is this pipeline's blaze. FOUR THINGS A READER SHOULD NOT HAVE TO RE-FETCH TO LEARN. (1) MARKER is a genuine coded domain whose codes ARE the words (Red/Yellow/Blue/Orange/Green/White/Other), like oprhp_trails' Blaze and unlike side_trails' integers, so no domain decode stands in front of reference/blaze_mapping.json; live values on the 5,286 rows are 2,929 blank or null, Yellow 704, Blue 692, Red 622, White 128, Other 97, Orange 78, Green 35, and one 'ORANGE AND RED' that DEC's own domain does not declare. (2) FOOT reads Y on 4,050 rows and M on 1,236, and nothing else - see foot_allowed and foot_allowed_comment above. (3) THERE IS NO STATUS COLUMN, so every kept row exports as open under export_nearby_trails.py's DEFAULT_STATUS: DEC publishes no closure state here, and inventing one would be the failure that module's closure treatment exists to avoid. PUBLICUSE reads 'Y' on all 5,286, which is a layer-wide constant rather than a filter worth having. (4) IDS FALL BACK TO OBJECTID, because DEC spells the column GLOBALID and lib/feature_id.py looks for GlobalID - the ids are unique across the fetched 5,286 and stable within a fetch, but a DEC republish that renumbers OBJECTIDs would renumber ours; the stable column is there for the taking if that ever bites. FRESHNESS: no editingInfo (a classic on-prem MapServer), so fetch_external_layers.py's change-aware skip cannot fire for this entry and it is re-fetched every run - accepted rather than fixed, because the layer is 13 MB and the alternative is machinery nothing else needs. The marker the survey identified does work and costs one request: max(UPDATED) via outStatistics answered in 0.5 s on 2026-08-25 and returned 2026-08-20. THE LAYER'S OWN SCOPE, stated because the name oversells it: 'Hiking Trails' is DEC's per-use split, so a row is here because foot travel is allowed on it, not because it is a footpath - 446 rows are ASSET 'SNOWMOBILE TRAIL' with FOOT 'Y', 456 are unpaved roads, and they are walkable corridors on DEC land rather than mistakes. UNIT mixes preserve codes (AFP 2,293, CFP 312) with hundreds of per-county state-forest codes and some dirt (blank, misspellings), exactly as the survey warned; nothing filters on it, per #1019.

sources.title: NYS DEC Lean-tos (statewide)
sources.steward: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation
sources.licence: See dec_licence below - the same footing dec_hiking_trails ships on, and not a new grant. DEC states no terms of their own: copyrightText is empty on every one of these services and on each layer, read live 2026-08-27, and an on-prem MapServer has no AGOL item carrying terms either. So these ship on the maintainer's authorisation of 2026-08-25, extended to POIs by their 2026-08-27 decision to act on POI_COVERAGE_SURVEY.md. The ask recorded in NYC_SOURCE_SURVEY.md §10(c) - bundle DEC into the OPRHP outreach, one state, two agencies - is still open and is made no less live by this registration.
sources.attribution: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation
sources.discovered_via: POI_COVERAGE_SURVEY.md §2's measured finding that DEC republishes its PUBLICUSE='Y' slice as small per-type services, and §9's follow-up #1 naming them - acted on under #1097 on the maintainer's 2026-08-27 decision. Registered by hand: discover_sources.py walks ATC's Experience Builder app and these are on DEC's own on-prem server.
sources.notes: 315 lean-tos statewide, counted live 2026-08-27. THE COUNT IS THE POINT OF USING THIS SERVICE RATHER THAN THE BIG LAYER: dec_backcountry_features carries 325 LEAN-TO rows of which exactly 315 read PUBLICUSE 'Y', so this service IS DEC's own public slice and using it means shipping DEC's curation instead of re-deriving it (POI_COVERAGE_SURVEY.md §2 has the same check on six other services - four exact, three within five features). NO CAPACITY FIELD, which decides how a card may speak: fields are UNIT/FACILITY/NAME/ASSET/DESCRIP/NOTES/ACCESSIBLE/UPDATED/PHOTO_LINK and nothing states how many the shelter sleeps, so a DEC shelter exports without capacity - absent meaning unknown, never zero (CLAUDE.md, 'Omit rather than guess'). Two fields that look useful and are not: PHOTO_LINK points at an internal drive (M:\DLF\...) that resolves from inside DEC only, and NOTES carries DEC's '-99' null sentinel on some rows. REGISTERED AS LAYER 0 ONLY, and layer 1 of the same service is deliberately left out: it is the conservation-easement variant, assets on private land the public holds access rights over (fields CE_ASSET_U and PUBRIGHTS, absent from layer 0). Measured 2026-08-27 it is small - 1 lean-to, 10 parking areas - and it is the same shape dil_trails layer 3 has, which dec_hiking_trails also declined when it registered layer 2 alone. Following that precedent rather than inventing a second one; an easement asset carries an access question layer 0's state land does not, and it wants its own decision rather than a ride along with this.

freshness.notes: An on-prem MapServer exposes no editingInfo, so fetch_external_layers.py's change check cannot read a last-edit date here and re-fetches this layer on every run - the same state dec_hiking_trails is in, recorded rather than fixed. The substitute marker is a max(UPDATED) statistics query, which the big layer answers as 2026-08-18 (read 2026-08-27, over 21,445 of 21,468 dated rows). Nothing reads this block yet.

sources.public_field_comment: PUBLICUSE FILTERS on every DEC layer - an N row is not a weaker POI, it is an internal maintenance asset (the big layer's N side is 4,290 culverts, gates and sign posts). These per-type services are already DEC's own Y slice, so the filter is expected to drop nothing here; it is applied anyway so that a service DEC later widens cannot quietly bring internal assets with it. export_nearby_poi.py prints what it drops.

sources.notes: 1,852 parking areas statewide, counted live 2026-08-27, against 1,857 parking-shaped rows flagged PUBLICUSE 'Y' in the big layer - the third and widest of the near-misses, five features. Mixed surface and purpose (UNPAVED PARKING LOT dominates at 2,067 of the big layer's parking rows, with 78 DESIGNATED HUNTER PARKING AREA among them), and the layer states no seasonal access - one sampled easement row read 'SEASONALLY OPEN MAY 1 TO SEPT 30' in free-text NOTES, so seasonality exists in DEC's data as prose and not as a field. REGISTERED AS LAYER 0 ONLY, and layer 1 of the same service is deliberately left out: it is the conservation-easement variant, assets on private land the public holds access rights over (fields CE_ASSET_U and PUBRIGHTS, absent from layer 0). Measured 2026-08-27 it is small - 1 lean-to, 10 parking areas - and it is the same shape dil_trails layer 3 has, which dec_hiking_trails also declined when it registered layer 2 alone. Following that precedent rather than inventing a second one; an easement asset carries an access question layer 0's state land does not, and it wants its own decision rather than a ride along with this.

freshness.notes: An on-prem MapServer exposes no editingInfo, so fetch_external_layers.py's change check cannot read a last-edit date here and re-fetches this layer on every run - the same state dec_hiking_trails is in, recorded rather than fixed. The substitute marker is a max(UPDATED) statistics query, which the big layer answers as 2026-08-18 (read 2026-08-27, over 21,445 of 21,468 dated rows). Nothing reads this block yet.

sources.public_field_comment: PUBLICUSE FILTERS on every DEC layer - an N row is not a weaker POI, it is an internal maintenance asset (the big layer's N side is 4,290 culverts, gates and sign posts). These per-type services are already DEC's own Y slice, so the filter is expected to drop nothing here; it is applied anyway so that a service DEC later widens cannot quietly bring internal assets with it. export_nearby_poi.py prints what it drops.

sources.title: NYS DEC Back Country Features (statewide asset inventory)
sources.steward: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation
sources.licence: See dec_licence below - the same footing dec_hiking_trails ships on, and not a new grant. DEC states no terms of their own: copyrightText is empty on every one of these services and on each layer, read live 2026-08-27, and an on-prem MapServer has no AGOL item carrying terms either. So these ship on the maintainer's authorisation of 2026-08-25, extended to POIs by their 2026-08-27 decision to act on POI_COVERAGE_SURVEY.md. The ask recorded in NYC_SOURCE_SURVEY.md §10(c) - bundle DEC into the OPRHP outreach, one state, two agencies - is still open and is made no less live by this registration.
sources.attribution: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation
sources.discovered_via: NYC_SOURCE_SURVEY.md §3 named this layer on 2026-08-18 and left it unregistered; POI_COVERAGE_SURVEY.md §1 measured what is actually in it on 2026-08-27, and #1097 registers it for the two POI types DEC publishes no per-type service for. Registered by hand.
sources.notes: 21,468 points, counted live 2026-08-27. REGISTERED FOR EXACTLY TWO POI TYPES - privy and crossing, and since #1674 withdrew the crossing type, only privy ships from it - and deliberately not for the four DEC publishes per-type services for, which are registered separately above. THIS IS NOT A POI LAYER and must not be read as one: DEC's own description calls it 'Point data locating and differentiating assets on state lands... man-made items, which require periodic maintenance or inspection', its largest single value is CULVERT at 4,290 features, and 68% of it is things no hiker wants a pin for. export_nearby_poi.py takes it through a value allowlist plus PUBLICUSE, never a type-prefix match. `ASSET` is free text with 234 values as stored and 223 after trimming - the 12 whitespace variants include 'FORD ' beside 'FORD' and a bare ' ' on 86 rows - and carries DEC's own misspellings ('PRIMATIVE CAMPSITE'), so any match on it is case-insensitive and stripped. PUBLICUSE splits the layer 7,645 Y / 13,823 N and is the only reason this layer is publishable at all. WHAT IS EXCLUDED AND WHY IT STAYS EXCLUDED: 98 rows across 27 values are PROPOSED assets ('PROPOSED LEAN-TO' x11, 'PROPOSED PIT PRIVY' x5) and are dropped - a hiker who walks to a proposed lean-to finds trees; the 4,290 culverts are not crossings, being pipes under the tread rather than things anyone walks over; and NO WATER SHIPS FROM THIS LAYER OR ANY DEC LAYER, which is a measured refusal rather than an omission - see dec_water_holdback below.

freshness.notes: max(UPDATED) across the layer, read 2026-08-27 over the 21,445 of 21,468 rows that carry a date (the range runs back to 2002-08-24). An on-prem MapServer has no editingInfo, so this substitute is the only freshness signal the layer offers. Nothing reads it automatically; changing `recorded` is how a person acknowledges having looked.

The host's robots.txt answered 200 and disallows nothing this URL reaches, and asks no Crawl-delay. THE FEED IS WHAT ITS HOST SERVES, which may be a window of the show: an episode's absence is never its removal. The audio is never fetched: an <enclosure> lands as its URL, length and type.
sources.reaches_hikers_comment: Registered and extracted, staged through its generated base model, and read by no mart: the podcasts mart is reference/podcast_episodes.json's editorial picks (_shared/podcasts/), and which of a feed's episodes a hike offers is a person's choice that file records. So nothing of this row reaches a phone, and it stays false until the maintainer decides whether a club's own show joins that list (decision 63 turns a layer true once its rules are in dbt and tested; a podcast has no such rule yet).

sources.title: National Forest System Trails (USFS, nationwide)
sources.licence: PUBLIC DOMAIN, on the maintainer's adoption of 17 U.S.C. 105 (2026-09-02: "Move the usfs licence to the public domain"). A work prepared by an officer or employee of the U.S. Government as part of their official duties is not subject to domestic copyright, so there is nothing here for the Forest Service to grant or withhold - which is why this is `stated_by_org` and not `maintainer_authorisation`. See usfs_licence below for what that does and does not cover.
sources.discovered_via: Probed directly under https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/1207 - the maintainer asked for the White Mountains' trail sources, and the USFS Enterprise Data Warehouse is the Forest Service's own public REST endpoint. Registered by hand: discover_sources.py walks ATC's Experience Builder app and this is an on-prem ArcGIS server behind no AGOL item, so there is nothing for it to discover. Found by listing apps.fs.usda.gov/arcx/rest/services/EDW and filtering its service names.
sources.notes: 78,101 TERRA polyline segments nationwide of 86,329 total (SNOW 8,152, WATER 76), measured live 2026-09-02 by group-by statistics. THE WHITE MOUNTAINS ARE WHERE THIS WAS FOUND AND NOT WHAT IT COVERS: this entry was registered under #1207, whose subject was the Whites, and the maintainer's decision that day was to ship the organization whole rather than clip it - the same call export_nearby_trails.py's docstring records for DEC and NYNJTC ('Don't limit data from orgs based on geography'). The Whites are selectable inside it as admin_org LIKE '0922%' (Region 09, Forest 22), which is 2,093 segments and 1,548.171 gis_miles, of which 1,544 are TERRA - and pipeline/WHITE_MOUNTAINS_SOURCE_SURVEY.md is the survey those numbers come from. NOTHING FILTERS ON admin_org: an earlier version of this entry carried `scope_field`/`scope_filter` keys naming that expression, and they were REMOVED because nothing read them - fetch_external_layers.py fetches whole layers and had no idea they existed, so they were decoration that would have read as an enforced limit. THREE THINGS A READER SHOULD NOT HAVE TO RE-FETCH. (1) trail_type is the walkability filter and foot_allowed_comment above is why. (2) national_trail_designation looks like an A.T. filter and is @unvalidated - see national_trail_designation_comment. (3) NO BLAZE FIELD AT ALL: the Forest Service publishes trail_surface, trail_class and a large per-use matrix, and no paint colour anywhere in the 100-odd columns, so this entry carries no blaze_field - an absence stated rather than a colour guessed. Searching trail_name for 'APPALACHIAN' returns 0 rows: the A.T. is present under its local trail names, which is correct for the Whites. FRESHNESS: no editingInfo (an on-prem ArcGIS server) and no date column either - the only date-ish field in the schema is accessibility_status, which is not one. See the freshness block for the ETag that is the only marker available and why it is tagged unvalidated.
sources.national_trail_designation_comment: @unvalidated, BUT MUCH BETTER EVIDENCED THAN WHEN THIS ENTRY WAS FIRST WRITTEN - and the change is a correction of this note's own over-caution, recorded rather than swapped. national_trail_designation is an integer whose `domain` reads null on the live field metadata (2026-09-02), so the Forest Service publishes no decode. WMNF distribution, measured 2026-09-02: code 1 on 1,962 segments (1,397.866 mi), code 2 on 8 (6.058 mi), code 3 on 123 (144.247 mi). THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS NOTE SAID CODE 3 'IS NOT AN A.T. FILTER', on the strength of GREAT GULF and MADISON GULF carrying it. AN INDEPENDENT SOURCE NOW SAYS OTHERWISE. nh_granit_trails covers the same ground from a different publisher, and its white-blazed set - 62 rows, 61 of them TRAILSYS 'Appalachian Trail' - names essentially the same trails code 3 does: Beaver Brook, Benton, Carter-Moriah, Cascade Brook, Centennial, Crawford Path, Ethan Pond, Fishin' Jimmy, Franconia Ridge, Garfield Ridge, Glencliff, Gulfside, Kenduskeag, Kinsman Ridge, Liberty Spring - AND GREAT GULF AMONG THEM. So the row that was this note's main counter-example is grouped with the A.T. by BOTH publishers independently, which makes it far likelier that code 3 means the Appalachian National Scenic Trail and that Great Gulf is a corridor/adjacency call the two agencies happen to share, than that two unrelated sources made the same mistake. IT IS STILL @unvalidated, and the tag stays for a reason that has not moved: the Forest Service documents nothing, so this is a correlation between two undocumented columns rather than a decode of either. CRAWFORD PATH also still splits across codes 1, 2 AND 3, which no 'code 3 = the A.T.' reading explains. What would settle it: the Forest Service's data dictionary for the TrailNFS publish schema. What to do meanwhile: do not route on it. A hiker's A.T. route comes from ATC's own centerline, which this pipeline already ships and which is authoritative for exactly this question.

freshness.notes: @unvalidated AS A DATA-CHANGE SIGNAL. An on-prem ArcGIS server exposes no editingInfo, so fetch_external_layers.py's change-aware skip cannot fire for this entry - the state dec_hiking_trails is already in, recorded rather than fixed. This layer is WORSE than DEC's in one specific way: DEC has an UPDATED column, so a max(UPDATED) statistics query is a real substitute marker, and the TrailNFS schema has no date column at all. What is left is a STRONG ETag on the service description document, read 2026-09-02 as "1a7709d0" - the same marker shape check_freshness.py already compares verbatim for ATC's and NYNJTC's feeds. It is unvalidated because it is an ETag on the METADATA, and nothing has established that it moves when the FEATURES move: it could sit still across a full republish, or churn on a server restart. What would settle it: recording this value and re-reading it across a known USFS publish cycle. Nothing reads this block yet.

sources.foot_allowed_comment: WHY trail_type IS THE foot_field HERE, when on other sources that slot holds an actual foot column. export_nearby_trails.py's foot_field/foot_allowed pair means 'the field that decides whether you can walk this, and the values that say yes'. For OPRHP and DEC that is a per-use foot column. USFS publishes its trails split by MEDIUM instead: measured nationwide 2026-09-02, trail_type reads TERRA on 78,101 rows, SNOW on 8,152 and WATER on 76. The 8,228 non-TERRA rows are snowmobile and paddle corridors - a first page of WMNF results is HIX MTN RD SNOMO, BERRY FARM SNOMO, ROSEBROOK SNOMO - so TERRA is exactly the walkable set and the drop reason this prints ('not a foot trail: trail_type=SNOW') is true as written. WHY NOT hiker_pedestrian_managed, WHICH IS THE OBVIOUS CANDIDATE AND IS A TRAP. It is a SEASON STRING ('01/01-12/31'), not a flag, so it cannot be an allowed-set at all - and it is NULL on 35,667 of the 78,101 TERRA rows. Requiring it would delete 46% of the Forest Service's terrestrial trail inventory. Absent is unrecorded, not prohibited, which is the same lesson dec_hiking_trails' foot_allowed_comment records for DEC's `M` and nh_granit_trails' foot_comment records for GRANIT's blank PED - three sources, three vocabularies, one mistake. AND THE LAYER ESSENTIALLY NEVER PROHIBITS FOOT TRAVEL: 78,064 of the 78,101 TERRA rows carry at least one populated hiker_pedestrian_* column, and hiker_pedestrian_restricted reads the literal string 'N/A' on 399 of a 400-row sample of the rows where it is set. So there is no prohibition signal to honour even if one were wanted. WHAT CHANGED ON 2026-09-28 (#1711): motorized trails are now excluded - see excluded_when_comment. WHAT IS STILL LEFT UNDONE: this export cannot tell a trail MANAGED for hikers from one where hiking is merely accepted, and it keeps bicycle and pack-and-saddle trails that also allow foot travel, because a trail a hiker may walk is walkable ground.
sources.excluded_when_comment: THE MAINTAINER'S DECISION OF 2026-09-28 (#1711): 'remove USFS motorized trails nationwide. Only include hiking trails.' terra_motorized is a three-value column, measured live 2026-09-28 across trail_type TERRA nationwide: 'N' 45,151 rows / 74,529 gis_miles, 'Y' 23,195 / 29,199, 'N/A' 9,810 / 21,332. WHAT 'Y' MEANS, reasoned rather than published (the field's domain reads null): allowed_terra_use is a string of use codes, and every 'Y' row carries a 4, 5 or 6 in it - motorcycle, ATV, 4WD - while no 'N' row does, apart from about 1,470 'Y' rows (125 mi) whose codes are only 3, 31 or 321, which the Forest Service still flags motorized and which go with the rest. WHAT GOES WITH IT, known and accepted: the Great Western Trail and its ATV/OHV alternates (254 mi), which are motorized routes by design, and about 74 mi of the Continental Divide Trail where it shares tread with motorized routes (CONTINENTAL DIVIDE NST, MONARCH CREST-CDNST, CDNST - COCHETOPA ROADS, CONTINENTAL DIVIDE ATV). The CDT will show gaps there. WHY 'N/A' IS KEPT: every use column on those 9,810 rows is empty, so nothing says they are NOT hiking trails - and they include about 570 mi of the Pacific Crest Trail, the Sheltowee Trace (287 mi), the Ouachita NRT (187 mi), the Arizona Trail (143 mi) and the Tahoe Rim Trail (111 mi). Dropping them would delete real hiking trails on the strength of an absence, which is the mistake foot_allowed_comment already records for hiker_pedestrian_managed. Adding 'N/A' to this list is the one-line reversal if the maintainer wants it.
sources.blaze_default_comment: THE FOREST SERVICE PUBLISHES NO BLAZE COLUMN AT ALL - not a blank one, none - across the 100-odd fields of the TrailNFS publish schema, checked against the live field list 2026-09-02. So this states the absence rather than asserting a paint, exactly as nynjtc_highlands_trail's blaze_default does for the same reason. IT IS 'Unknown' AND NOT 'None', AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE POINT: 'None' means a CONFIRMED unblazed trail (the client renders it 'Unblazed'), which is what nh_granit_trails' blank BLAZE earns because GRANIT does record blazes where they exist and records none here. USFS records nothing either way, so the honest word is 'Blaze not recorded'. Two sources covering the same White Mountains ground, two different absences, and collapsing them would tell a hiker the Forest Service had checked. It also has a mechanical job: network_line_sources() identifies a trail-LINE source by the presence of blaze_field or blaze_default, so without this key export_nearby_trails.py would skip this layer entirely as if it were a points layer - which it did, until a test caught it.

sources.licence: PUBLIC DOMAIN, on the maintainer's adoption of 17 U.S.C. 105 (2026-09-02: "Move the usfs licence to the public domain"). A work prepared by an officer or employee of the U.S. Government as part of their official duties is not subject to domestic copyright, so there is nothing here for the Forest Service to grant or withhold - which is why this is `stated_by_org` and not `maintainer_authorisation`. See usfs_licence below for what that does and does not cover.
sources.discovered_via: Probed under https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/1207 alongside usfs_trails, by listing apps.fs.usda.gov/arcx/rest/services/EDW for recreation services. Three candidates were compared on the same Whites bounding box (2026-09-02): EDW_RecreationOpportunities_01 returned 258 points, EDW_InfraRecreationSites_01 returned 316, and this one returned 318 with a site_type column the other two lack. Registered by hand, for the same reason usfs_trails is.
sources.notes: 31,405 point features nationwide, measured live 2026-09-02 by group-by statistics on site_type. The types this pipeline reads, with their nationwide counts: TRAILHEAD 7,358 (-> parking, and the single most useful thing either USFS layer holds for a hiker), CAMPGROUND 4,183 and GROUP CAMPGROUND 422 (-> campsite), OBSERVATION SITE 636 (-> viewpoint). Everything else is deliberately unmapped in export_nearby_poi.py's USFS_SITE_TYPES. THE BIG ONE THAT DOES NOT SHIP IS 'CAMPING AREA', 10,783 ROWS - the largest site_type in the layer, larger than every campground in the national forest system put together. It is DISPERSED CAMPING and publishing it would break an editorial holdback this project already made. See usfs_dispersed_camping_holdback for the evidence and the argument. Also unmapped and worth naming so nobody re-derives them: LOOKOUT/CABIN 815 (a fire lookout or a rentable cabin is not a trail shelter - see the poi_coverage shelter verdict), HOTEL/LODGE/RESORT 164 (where AMC's huts would be if they are in any public dataset - unprobed, pipeline/WHITE_MOUNTAINS_SOURCE_SURVEY.md section 6(f)), and the ski, boating, fishing, target-range and OHV-staging types, none of which is a POI_TYPE. THE LAYER PUBLISHES NO WATER AND NO PRIVIES: no site_type of either shape exists. total_capacity and fee_charged exist as columns and were NOT profiled. THE WHITE MOUNTAINS SUBSET, since #1207 is where this came from: 335 sites on managing_org LIKE '0922%', returned whole in one page - 187 TRAILHEAD, 53 CAMPGROUND, 20 OBSERVATION SITE, 16 HOTEL/LODGE/RESORT, 15 PICNIC SITE, 12 CAMPING AREA, 6 LOOKOUT/CABIN and a tail. Note the inversion that made the dispersed question visible: in the Whites CAMPGROUND outnumbers CAMPING AREA 53 to 12, and nationwide CAMPING AREA outnumbers CAMPGROUND 10,783 to 4,183.

freshness.notes: No editingInfo and no date column, the same as usfs_trails - see that entry's freshness block for the full argument and for the service-metadata ETag that is the only marker the EDW server offers. Nothing reads this block yet.

sources.field_comment: id_field is spelled LOWERCASE 'objectid' because the EDW layer spells it that way - export_nearby_poi.py defaults to 'OBJECTID' and would have fallen through to a null id on every row. The layer publishes no GlobalID and no public/visitor flag, so there is no public_field here: unlike DEC's PUBLICUSE and OPRHP's ParksApp, the Forest Service offers nothing to filter or lower confidence on, and inventing one would be worse than having none.

sources.terms: None read for these pages beyond the federal public-domain reading in `licence`.

freshness.notes: The page's validators are not trusted (extract/_notices.py's PageNotice, trust_validators off): every hourly run reads it, one request, and FRESH only when the landed row hashes as the last load's. Two reads on 2026-10-03, about ten minutes apart, landed the same region_sha256, so the region carries no per-render token (Measured, twice). The listing sends no ETag and no Last-Modified (2026-10-03).

sources.notes: One row: the page's notice (extract/_notices.py's PageNotice), keyed by `url`. Read 2026-10-03: the USFS alerts template every forest shares, 16 alert cards under /alerts/<slug>, levels critical 1, fire-restriction 1, caution 1, information 13, beside the four-card level legend, no pager and no feed. The reader's region is <main>, its title the page's <h1> 'Alerts' (expect_title holds it), and no date: the page states none of its own, and each card's 'Alert Start Date' is an item's, so date_pattern is off. A per-alert reader on the stable slug links is the next step phase A's evidence supports. Among them 'Citico Creek Flood Closure' (critical) and 'Roan Mountain Fire Restrictions'.

sources.title: NJ State Park Service Trails (NJDEP Bureau of GIS, Features/Land layer 63)
sources.steward: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection
sources.licence: See njdep_licence below. Registered UNRESOLVED on 2026-09-09 (#1293): NJDEP's on-prem service states only copyrightText 'NJDEP' and no terms of its own (read live 2026-09-09), and the NJDEP Data Distribution Agreement is stated on the Forum item beside it (nj_statewide_trails), owned by the same NJDEPBGIS account - so the agreement is read as this layer's terms by inference from the owner, not from anything this service says. The agreement permits reuse on conditions, and two of the conditions need a deliberate act before anything ships: redistribution 'with all the metadata provided', and the credit/disclaimer wording verbatim on any map. That decision is the maintainer's and nothing here reaches a hiker until it is recorded.
sources.attribution: This (map/publication/report) was developed using New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection Geographic Information System digital data, but this secondary product has not been verified by NJDEP and is not state-authorized or endorsed.
sources.foot_comment: SET 2026-09-11, when the maintainer cleared this layer to reach hikers. The filter is the one this comment specified while the flag was shut, applied unchanged: HIKING_TRL reads 'Yes' on 3,226 rows, 'No' on 75 and null on 4 (measured 2026-09-09), which is the clean shape a foot_field wants - unlike nh_granit_trails' PED, whose blank meant unrecorded - so an allowlist on 'Yes' is sound here, and the 4 nulls are dropped and counted rather than assumed walkable, which is the conservative direction. MOTO_TRL 'Yes' on 35 rows is the motorized corridor this comment said a filter should drop, and excluded_when is what drops it - the same shape nh_granit_trails uses, and the maintainer's "It's OurHike, not OurBike" (2026-08-18). TRL_TYPE_S is 'Official' 3,112 / 'Connector' 193 and is deliberately NOT filtered on: both are trail a hiker walks, and dropping connectors would cut the links between the rest.

freshness.notes: @unvalidated AS A DATA-CHANGE SIGNAL, for usfs_trails' reason exactly: an on-prem ArcGIS server exposes no editingInfo, so fetch_external_layers.py's change-aware skip cannot fire for this entry, and the schema's only date column (SRCE_DATE) is a free-text string. What is left is the STRONG ETag on the layer description document ("a3ece85c", read 2026-09-09; the service document beside it reads "65e53daa"), which moves when the layer's metadata is re-published and may or may not move when its rows are edited. What would settle it: watching the two across an edit NJDEP announces.

sources.discovered_via: pipeline/NYC_SOURCE_SURVEY.md section 5 (2026-08-18) qualified it and nobody acted; the maintainer asked for its registration on 2026-09-09 under https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/1293, because #1290's New Jersey hikes are held without it. Registered by hand: discover_sources.py walks ATC's Experience Builder app and this is NJDEP's own on-prem server.
sources.notes: 3,305 polyline segments, measured live 2026-09-09 via returnCountOnly - 'over 1,000 miles of official recreational trails on lands owned and managed by New Jersey State Park Service', in the layer's own description, which also says the data 'is not intended for orienteering purposes' because of 'varying degrees of spatial accuracy and detail' between NJDEP staff, volunteers and non-profits who collected it. THE RICHEST BLAZE SCHEMA THIS PROJECT HAS SEEN, and the judgement it needed: three colour fields (TRL_COLOR, ALT_TRL_COLOR, PBN_COLOR) plus BLAZE_TYPE and BLAZE_DESC. TRL_COLOR is the blaze - 42 distinct values, the seven palette colours plus Teal on 2,299 rows (70%), 'Unmarked' 228, then paints the palette lacks (Gray 236, Lt Brown 173, Pink 94) and compounds ('Black/White' 37) - and reference/blaze_mapping.json's njdep_park_trails table records why it and not the other two. TRL_DIFF is NJDEP's own five levels (Easy 1,510, Moderate 884, Easy to Moderate 453, Difficult 259, Moderate to Difficult 103, Unknown 90) - the same shape as NYNJTC's five, which is worth knowing when the app's difficulty vocabulary is next discussed. NO editingInfo (on-prem), so the change-aware skip cannot fire; the ETag in `freshness` is the marker. WHAT IT WOULD ROUTE FOR #1290, probed 2026-09-09 as the segments within ~900 m of each held hike's trailhead: Mount Tammany 8 (Appalachian Trail, Blue Trail, Dunnfield Creek Trail, Mt. Tammany Trail), Swartswood's Duck Pond loop 9 (Emmons' Path, Passage, Sinkhole, Spring Lake), Wawayanda's Laurel Pond loop 7 (Banker, Cedar Swamp, Cherry Ridge), the State Line Trail 1 - and NOTHING at Ramapo Valley County Reservation, Schooley's Mountain County Park or the Palisades, which are county and PIPC ground and the statewide layer's question. A companion POI layer, 62 'Open Space (State Owned) Points of Interest', sits in the same folder; its count is unprobed and it is not registered (#1293's own scope).

sources.person_fields_comment: CREATED_USER and LAST_EDITED_USER are ArcGIS editor tracking: the account that created or last edited each row, found on this layer by a metadata read on 2026-10-03. extract/_kinds.py's PERSON_FIELDS drops them on every layer; listed here too so this row says which of its own columns never load.
sources.steward: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection
sources.licence: See njdep_licence below - the NJDEP Data Distribution Agreement is this item's own licenseInfo, read whole (1,968 characters) on 2026-09-09 and quoted there verbatim. Registered UNRESOLVED: the agreement permits reuse on conditions, and two of them need a deliberate act before anything ships - redistribution 'with all the metadata provided', and the credit/disclaimer wording verbatim on any map. THE STEWARD IS NJDEP AND THE LINES ARE NOT ALL NJDEP'S, and the difference matters for attribution: the item is 'a compilation of linear trail data provided by multiple agencies' - 166 distinct MANAGING_AGENCY values - 'accepted as is' by the Forum's task force, hosted and licensed by NJDEP's Bureau of GIS. The agreement is NJDEP's; the credit it requires names NJDEP; which county or trust drew a given line is the row's MANAGING_AGENCY, and a per-line attribution surface is a question this registration records rather than answers.
sources.attribution: This (map/publication/report) was developed using New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection Geographic Information System digital data, but this secondary product has not been verified by NJDEP and is not state-authorized or endorsed.
sources.foot_comment: SET 2026-09-11, when the maintainer cleared this layer to reach hikers, and it is the filter this comment specified while the flag was shut: TRAIL_TYPE in {off-road, connector, side path} AND HIKING != 'N'. WHAT IT DROPS, and why each matters more here than on any other registered layer (measured 2026-09-09): TRAIL_TYPE is 'on-road' on 1,085 rows, 'sidewalk' 50, 'crosswalk' 36, 'water' 19 (paddling trails) and 'parking' 9 - none of which is a trail a hiker walks, and build_trail_graph.py's own rule is that roads are not edges. HIKING is 'Y' 8,257 / 'U' 4,825 / 'N' 213, and the 'U' is UNRECORDED - the nh_granit_trails trap - so HIKING cannot be the allowlist and is used only to drop the explicit 'N'; TRAIL_TYPE, whose values are all populated, is the allowlist instead. ONE ROW BEYOND THE WRITTEN SPECIFICATION, said rather than slipped in: MOTORIZED_USE_ALLOWED 'Y' on 117 rows is dropped too. The specification named only TRAIL_TYPE and HIKING, but 'off-road' includes motorized off-road, so those 117 would otherwise have shipped as hiking line. Dropping on a positive motorized assertion is the precedent nh_granit_trails' excluded_when already sets, and the alternative is a motorized corridor drawn as trail - one of the four ways this app can hurt somebody. Reverse it here if that reading is wrong.
