trail_marks._the_nst_shield_question: @unvalidated WHICH SHIPPED MARKS ARE THE PRESCRIBED NATIONAL SCENIC TRAIL MARKER, AND WHETHER THAT MATTERS. Raised by review 2026-09-30, unresolved, and recorded here rather than smoothed over. FOUR of the marks in this block are the NST shield form - a rounded triangle with the trail's name arced above and 'NATIONAL SCENIC TRAIL' below: `at`, `net`, `iat` and `pct`. Three of those four have an 'Official Trail Marker' notice in the Federal Register (Appalachian and Ice Age 2000-03-28, New England 2021-06-28), which is the same instrument that keeps `pohe` and `natr` out. WHAT THE PCT CHECK ACTUALLY ESTABLISHED was narrower than it reads: it enumerated all 25 notices and reasoned about 5 of them - the 4 already treated as protected, plus the PCT's absence. The other 20 were never diffed against the rows that ship. THE A.T.'s IS NOT IN QUESTION: it is the repo owner's own file on their own decision and predates all of this, and the maintainer asked for it specifically to stay. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: read each of the 25 notices, list the trails, and diff that list against the slugs in this block - one pass, and it is the pass nobody has done. Until then do not read the `pct` row's insignia paragraph as having answered this for anything but the PCT.

organizations._comment: The registered organizations, by stable id (#929). SOURCE_REGISTRY.md: "`sources.json` therefore stores a stable steward id, not an address - `\"steward\": \"org:nynjtc\"` resolving to the backend record." This is that id, introduced as an ENTITY rather than as a per-source string, because `provider` already determines it one-to-one and thirty-three copies of a derivable value is thirty-three chances for one of them to be wrong. WHY IT IS WORTH HAVING AT ALL, stated because 'we already have `provider`' is the obvious objection: `provider` is a display string that has changed shape twice in this file's history (an abbreviation for ATC, four agency names for the drought monitor) and every join in the pipeline currently rests on one of those strings matching another one byte-for-byte. That has already failed silently once - see usdm_licence's `author_note`. An id is the thing that cannot be reworded. #929 calls this "what the client has been missing": `map/nearbyTrails.ts` keys ghosting off the pipeline's `source` because no feature carries a steward id, and `lib/source_registry.py`'s `poi_source_steward` exists purely to paper over twelve ATC entries that carry a `provider` and no `steward`. IDS ARE PERMANENT. Renaming one is a data migration, not an edit - a phone holding an older release joins on the id it was built with. tests/test_organizations.py pins the set both ways: every provider in `sources` has exactly one organization, and every organization has at least one source.

org:atc.name: Appalachian Trail Conservancy
org:atc.note: The A.T.'s route owner and the source of twelve of the registry's layers. `provider` is the three-letter form the registry has always used; the id is stable and the name is what a hiker reads.

org:gatc.name: Georgia Appalachian Trail Club
org:gatc.note: One of the thirty maintaining clubs, registered for its water-source PDF. Nothing of theirs reaches a hiker until they answer a redistribution ask.

org:nynjtc.name: New York-New Jersey Trail Conference
org:nynjtc.note: Maintains trails across the NY-NJ region. Two public trail extracts and their trail alerts ship on the maintainer's authorisation; the full network is deliberately withheld and is an agreement, not a scrape.

org:nysoprhp.name: New York State Office of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation
org:nysoprhp.note: The landowner inside Harriman, Fahnestock and every other state park the ring crosses. The only registered organization whose terms are STATED rather than authorised by the maintainer.

org:nysdec.name: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation
org:nysdec.note: The landowner on forest-preserve stretches, and the largest single block of layers after ATC's. Terms genuinely unstated; the ask is open (#1019).

org:mohonk.name: Mohonk Preserve
org:mohonk.note: A private preserve with a public trail extract. Terms unstated beyond a no-warranty disclaimer.

org:osm.name: OpenStreetMap contributors
org:osm.note: Not an organization with a steward to contact - a project with a licence. ODbL, and the attribution is a condition rather than a courtesy. `community` trust, the only source that carries it.

org:usgs.name: U.S. Geological Survey
org:usgs.note: Watched rather than fetched. Public-domain federal data, registered so that a change in it is noticed rather than discovered. Also registered for its points of interest under decision 54 (2026-10-03), at reaches_hikers: false.

org:ndmc.provider: National Drought Mitigation Center (UNL), USDA, NOAA, NASA
org:ndmc.name: National Drought Mitigation Center, University of Nebraska-Lincoln
org:ndmc.note: The U.S. Drought Monitor's polygons. The `provider` string names all four co-producing agencies because the DATASET is jointly produced; the `name` names the one organization that publishes it, which is also the `steward` the licence block joins on.

reaches_hikers_comment: Why every source entry carries `reaches_hikers` (#927). The sources screen names the organizations whose data is on a hiker's phone, under the terms each one set - so it has to know which registered sources actually SHIP, and that fact lived only in prose inside each entry's `licence` string ('fetched for REVIEW AND CROSS-CHECKS ONLY', 'nothing from this source reaches a published artifact until...'). A screen that decided by reading those sentences would print a licence claim for data nobody publishes the first time one was reworded. So it is a field: true means an exporter reads this source and its data reaches a release, false means registered-but-not-shipped, for any reason - review-only pending a licence answer (gatc_water_sources, every oprhp_*), watched-only (usgs_3dhp), or registered and not yet wired to anything (bridges, at_treadway, per pipeline/README.md). It is NOT a licence judgement and does not replace one: a source can be freely licensed and still not ship. export_sources.py refuses to run if any entry lacks the field, so a newly registered source cannot reach a hiker's screen by defaulting into it.
licence_basis_comment: WHAT A SOURCE'S LICENCE ACTUALLY RESTS ON, as a field rather than as prose (#929). Three values and they are not interchangeable: `stated_by_org` - the organization published terms of its own and they permit this (OPRHP's licenseInfo, ODbL, a federal public-domain work); `maintainer_authorisation` - the organization has stated nothing that reaches this use, and the maintainer authorised it as the person who carries the consequence. IT IS NOT A GRANT FROM THE ORGANIZATION and must never be rendered as one; `unresolved` - nobody has answered, and nothing ships. WHY IT IS A FIELD. Every one of these facts was already written down, in the per-source `licence` prose and the `<x>_licence` blocks - and only there. A screen or a report that wanted to say 'eleven of the thirty-three ship on your own authorisation rather than the org's terms' had to decide it by reading those sentences, which is exactly the failure `reaches_hikers_comment` records for the flag above: 'a screen that decided by reading those sentences would print a licence claim for data nobody publishes the first time one was reworded'. The same argument, one field over. IT IS NOT A JUDGEMENT ABOUT QUALITY and it does not replace the prose: the prose is where the reasoning, the dates, the read terms and the open questions live. This is one word saying which of the three shapes that reasoning has, so it can be counted. Measured 2026-08-27 against this file: 6 stated_by_org, 26 maintainer_authorisation, 1 unresolved. Re-measured 2026-09-08 (#1288): 8, 28 and 1 - nynjtc_long_path_guide was registered `unresolved` that morning and moved to `maintainer_authorisation` the same day on the maintainer's word (nynjtc_guide_licence); tests/test_organizations.py pins all three. A FOURTH VALUE, `public_gis`, has rows since 2026-10-03: decision 21a's presumption (pipeline/ELT.md, 'Who may publish', rule 3) that a GIS layer an organization publishes itself, anonymously, on a public endpoint is reusable for rendering with attribution. Like `maintainer_authorisation` it is the maintainer's reading, NOT A GRANT FROM THE ORGANIZATION; tests/test_organizations.py counts all four.

poi_coverage._comment: What each organization publishes for each of lib/poi_schema.POI_TYPES, and whether OurHike ships it (#1092). The maintainer's ask, 2026-08-27: "We don't have POI for the org's outside of ATC. Search those sources for the POI types we have... Maybe we need to track each of the POI types for the org, and whether or not it is provided." This block is the second half of that - the answer in a form a test can read, so "does DEC give us campsites" stops being a question the next session re-probes from scratch. pipeline/POI_COVERAGE_SURVEY.md is the evidence and the argument; spike_org_poi_coverage.py is the script every count here came from, re-runnable in one command. THE COUNTS ARE OF WHAT THE ORG PUBLISHES, NOT OF WHAT A HIKER WOULD SEE: nothing here is clipped to a corridor, deduped against ATC's POIs, or filtered to walkable ground, because this block is a survey of supply and those are ingest decisions belonging to per-org issues. `org_flags_public` is the subset the org's OWN publication flag marks as visitor-facing - DEC's PUBLICUSE, OPRHP's ParksApp - and it is the more honest of the two numbers wherever the two disagree. Twelve of these cells became `shipping` on 2026-08-27 (#1097, export_nearby_poi.py -> nearby_poi.geojson): six DEC types and six OPRHP ones, 8,480 features. Neither org's water is among them. tests/test_poi_coverage.py enforces that every provider in `sources` has a verdict for every POI type, from the vocabulary below: no blanks, the same discipline NYC_SOURCE_SURVEY.md §9 applies to licensing.

status_vocabulary.shipping: An exporter reads this and it reaches a published release today.
status_vocabulary.available: The org publishes it, measured, and nothing here ingests it yet. The count is the org's, not ours.
status_vocabulary.unsuitable: The org publishes something of this shape and it does not clear the bar - said with the evidence, never as a shrug. Reserved for cases where shipping the data would mislead a hiker rather than merely under-serve one.
status_vocabulary.absent: Probed on the date given, and the org publishes nothing of this type anywhere this survey could reach.
status_vocabulary.unprobed: Not yet looked at. A real answer, and the only one here that is an admission rather than a finding.

ATC.note: The baseline every other row is measured against, and it is not as tidy as 'ATC ships all eight' would suggest. Two of the eight it was measured against were not ATC's data at all: `water` is dominated by opentrail.org and OSM points, with ATC contributing synthesized low-confidence points from the Campsite_Sustainability_Index distances (export_poi.py's atc_csi), and `crossing` was USGS NHD's entirely until #1674 withdrew the type (ATC's own bridge layer is registered and still unread).

NYS OPRHP.note: The richest non-ATC source found, and the only org that publishes something for all eight types. One layer carries all of it: NY_State_Park_Facilities, 8,823 points, typed by a free-text `Sub_Asset` taking 158 distinct values (`Asset` is a coded integer 1-17 whose domain the service does not publish, so Sub_Asset is the only legible type). Registered since 2026-08-18 as oprhp_facilities with reaches_hikers false. TWO CAVEATS THAT APPLY TO EVERY ROW BELOW. (1) `Public` is not a filter: it reads Y on all 8,823 rows. `ParksApp` is the field that discriminates (5,822 Y / 3,000 N) and is what org_flags_public reports here. (2) `CollectedDate` spans 2006-05-10 to 2026-04-30 with 10 rows carrying a 9999-09-09 sentinel; the bulk was collected 2011-2021, so a facility's presence is better evidence than its currency.

NYS DEC.note: The maintainer's own example - "DEC has Shelters & Campsites mapped" - and it holds: 331 shelters and 2,315 campsites, more backcountry campsites than any other source here. What the example does not say is WHAT KIND OF LAYER they are in. dec_backcountry_features/MapServer/0 is 21,468 points typed by a free-text `ASSET` (234 values as stored, 223 after trimming - 'FORD ' sits beside 'FORD'), and DEC's own description of it reads: 'Point data locating and differentiating assets on state lands. Assets represented as point features are man-made items, which require periodic maintenance or inspection.' It is a maintenance inventory that happens to contain recreation facilities - 4,290 of its rows are culverts - not a POI layer. `PUBLICUSE` splits it 7,645 Y / 13,823 N and is DEC's own answer to what a visitor should see; org_flags_public reports it, and it is the number to build on. DEC ALSO PUBLISHES THE Y SLICE AS ITS OWN SMALL SERVICES, which is the practical finding here: dil/dil_land_assets_lean_to is 315 features against 315 LEAN-TO rows flagged Y, dil_land_assets_prm_cmp is 2,078 against 2,078, dil_land_assets_scenic_vista 134 against 134, dil_land_assets_visitor_center 5 against 5 - four exact matches. Three more are close rather than exact (parking 1,852 vs 1,857, firetower 35 vs 34, viewing_area 34 vs 33), so the rule is measured and not perfect. Registering the small per-type services buys DEC's own curation instead of re-deriving it. Note there is NO per-type service for privies or water. 98 rows across 27 values are PROPOSED assets ('PROPOSED LEAN-TO' x11, 'PROPOSED PIT PRIVY' x5) and are excluded from every count below: a hiker who walks to a proposed lean-to finds trees.

shelter.note: SHIPPING since 2026-08-27 (#1097), 315 features via export_nearby_poi.py. 315 lean-tos, DEC's own PUBLICUSE='Y' service rather than the big layer's 325 rows. 331 - 325 'LEAN-TO' and 6 'SHELTER'; 321 flagged public. The Catskills' and Adirondacks' shelter network, and the largest non-ATC shelter source found. NO CAPACITY FIELD: the layer carries NAME/DESCRIP/NOTES/ACCESSIBLE/UPDATED and nothing about how many sleep there, so a DEC shelter would export without capacity - absent meaning unknown, per CLAUDE.md, never a guess. Also excludes 11 'PROPOSED LEAN-TO'. dil/dil_land_assets_lean_to is the same 315 rows as a standalone service.

campsite.note: SHIPPING since 2026-08-27 (#1097), 2,077 features via export_nearby_poi.py. 2,077 of DEC's 2,078 published primitive campsites - one row arrives with an empty coordinate array and is dropped rather than published at 0,0. 2,315 - 1,754 'PRIMITIVE TENT SITE', 548 'PRIMITIVE CAMPSITE', 8 'CAMPSITE', 5 'PRIMATIVE CAMPSITE' (DEC's own misspelling, kept because the rows are real); 2,091 flagged public. These are genuine backcountry sites, unlike OPRHP's drive-in campgrounds. dil/dil_land_assets_prm_cmp publishes the 2,078-row public slice on its own.

water.note: DECIDED 2026-08-27, and the decision was the maintainer's on reading this survey: "Lets not use water from DEC". Nothing in #1097 ships it, sources.json's `dec_water_holdback` carries the evidence beside the sources themselves, and export_nearby_poi.py's allowlist is what mechanically keeps it out. THE ONE ROW IN THIS BLOCK THAT IS A REFUSAL, and it closes NYC_SOURCE_SURVEY.md §10(g)'s DEC half. DEC's only plumbed-water asset type is 'WATER SUPPLY SYSTEM', 23 features, and ZERO of them are flagged PUBLICUSE Y - DEC's own answer is that none of it is for visitors. Sampling 14 of them found real water spigots beside a 'Water Storage Tank', an 'Underground Water Line', and a drilled well whose own NOTES read 'Not Approved For Human Consum[ption]'. The values that sound like water are worse: 207 'WATERHOLE' are fire-and-wildlife impoundments ('Wetland Pool', 'Made by Tioga County SWCD in 2016'), 97 'WELL' are dominated by NATURAL GAS WELLS and historic stacked-stone wells, 4 'CISTERN' are CCC-era fire cisterns, and 19 'SPRING' include one described as 'Unnoffical Unsanctioned Traditional Public Wa[ter]' and one 'Untested'. All 350 of those are PUBLICUSE N as well. Publishing any of it as drinking water would be the failure FEATURES.md names - a confidently wrong prediction is more dangerous than an honest unknown - so DEC is not a water source and this row should not be reopened without new data from DEC rather than a new reading of this one.

water.note: 21 water sources, on the narrowest rule in lib/nynjtc_long_path_guide.py: a spring named in the water sense, or water said outright ('a dependable source of water', 'last sure water before Big Hill Shelter', a park or snack bar listing water among its amenities). A season ('in the spring'), a spring house, a road named Springs and 'was the water source for the Kaatz mansion' are refused by pattern, and 'crosses a stream' - said 178 times on the forty pages - is never read as water on its own. Every one of the 21 was read in full on 2026-09-08 (the spike prints the list). What the guide says about reliability rides on the record in the cautious direction: 'seasonal ... reliable in all but the driest times' is unreliable. All placed by mile (CONFIDENCE_LOW); none carries coordinates. THIS IS THE SAFETY PATH, and it ships because somebody decided to: the maintainer's authorisation of 2026-09-08 (nynjtc_guide_licence) was given with the pull request body's statement that every one of these is CONFIDENCE_LOW, mile-placed and carries the guide's reliability word in front of them. The map draws a low-confidence pin with a broken rim, the card says the position is estimated, and the legend's 'Verified?' filter removes them - the schema's existing mechanism for 'real, but nobody has surveyed it'.

water.unregistered_source: MOVED HERE FROM THE crossing CELL when #1674 withdrew that type: the finding outlived it, because the same unregistered NHD download is behind site water. FOUND BY tests/test_poi_coverage.py WHILE WRITING THIS BLOCK, and left as a finding rather than fixed here. USGS's only registered entry is usgs_3dhp, kind watched_only, reaches_hikers false - a deliberate WATCH on the successor dataset, explicitly 'nothing fetches this'. The data that actually ships is the retired NHD, pulled as bulk HU4 GeoPackages from prd-tnm.s3.amazonaws.com/StagedProducts/Hydrography/NHD/ by fetch_trail_water.py, and it has no entry in `sources` at all. So the registry cannot say USGS reaches hikers, and export_sources.py cannot name them, even though NHD geometry is behind part of the water layer. reaches_hikers_comment calls that field the record of 'which registered sources actually SHIP'; this is data that ships without being registered, which is the one case the field cannot express. USFS.note: Probed for https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/1207, which began as a White Mountains question and ended as a nationwide registration - the maintainer's call that day was to ship the organization whole rather than clip it to the region that prompted it. Every verdict here therefore counts the NATIONWIDE layer, like the DEC and OPRHP rows and unlike the first draft of this block, which counted only White Mountain National Forest. The trails layer publishes no points at all, so all nine verdicts come from usfs_rec_sites' recreation sites - 31,405 on 2026-09-02, 31,406 on the 2026-09-04 re-run. Three types ship (trailhead, campsite, viewpoint); the strong result is 7,358 trailheads, which shipped as `parking` until https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/1218 moved them; the uncomfortable one is that the layer's LARGEST type is dispersed camping and is held back - see usfs_dispersed_camping_holdback.

shelter.note: THE FOREST SERVICE PUBLISHES NO TRAIL SHELTER TYPE. The nearest candidate is 815 rows of site_type 'LOOKOUT/CABIN', and a fire lookout or a rentable forest cabin is not what a hiker means by a shelter - it is not open, not free, and in the rental case needs a reservation months out. Shipping those as poi_type shelter would tell a hiker walking into weather that there is a roof ahead they cannot use, which is why this is 'unsuitable' rather than 'available': the data is real and the reading would mislead. What was NOT done, and would be the next step if this mattered: the rows' individual site_name and development_scale values were not examined, so whether any one of them is in fact a backcountry shelter is unknown. Counts are nationwide by group-by statistics on site_type over the layer's 31,405 rows, measured 2026-09-02; the White Mountains subset that prompted the registration is in usfs_rec_sites' notes.

campsite.note: 4,605 developed campgrounds ship as of 2026-09-02 (#1207): CAMPGROUND 4,183 plus GROUP CAMPGROUND 422, via export_nearby_poi.py's USFS_SITE_TYPES. THE COUNT IS DELIBERATELY NOT THE LAYER'S CAMPING TOTAL. 'CAMPING AREA' is 10,783 further rows - the largest site_type in the layer - and it is DISPERSED camping: development_scale 0 on 8,135 of them, names like 'RD 614 SITE 13' and 'FS1302-03'. It is held back under the same argument SOURCE_SURVEY.md section 3b holds back ATC's 2,333 user-created campsites, and sources.json's usfs_dispersed_camping_holdback carries the evidence. A CAVEAT ON WHAT DOES SHIP, because the number is not the whole truth either: these are drive-up campgrounds with fee envelopes, not the backcountry sites a hiker on a ridge is looking for, and they sit under the same pin as ATC's A.T. campsites. That is a POI_DEDUPLICATION and presentation question this registration does not answer. Counts are nationwide by group-by statistics on site_type over the layer's 31,405 rows, measured 2026-09-02; the White Mountains subset that prompted the registration is in usfs_rec_sites' notes.

parking.note: ABSENT, and this cell read `shipping` for sixteen days on the strength of one mapping. site_type 'TRAILHEAD' was the only value in USFS_SITE_TYPES pointing at parking, and https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/1218 moved it to poi_type trailhead - so this organization now publishes no parking at all. That is a MEASUREMENT and not a side effect: #1218 refused to close on the White Mountains census (335 rows of 31,405) that pointed this way, so the nationwide group-by was re-run 2026-09-04 and there is no `PARKING` site_type among the 33. The nearest are SNOWPARK 318, OHV STAGING AREA 181 and DAY USE AREA 1,034, none of which is a parking lot - this is a recreation-SITES layer, and a parking lot is not a recreation site, so the absence is structural rather than a gap in what the Forest Service publishes. A hiker looking for where to leave the car in a national forest is not served by this layer and is not served by pretending a trailhead is one. Counts are nationwide by group-by statistics on site_type, re-run 2026-09-04 for https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/1218: 33 distinct values over 31,406 features (31,405 on 2026-09-02 - the layer gained one row in two days).

privy.note: No privy or toilet site_type among the 31,405. Counts are nationwide by group-by statistics on site_type over the layer's 31,405 rows, measured 2026-09-02; the White Mountains subset that prompted the registration is in usfs_rec_sites' notes.

water.note: SHIPPING SINCE 2026-09-15 (#1461) AS UNKNOWN-STATUS POINTS, and what follows is the refusal it reverses - kept whole rather than rewritten, because only ONE of its two blockers is gone and the other is now carried by `confidence_floor` rather than by holding the layer back. The TYPE problem is solved: PIP element names decode A-F, so nyc_drinking_fountains ships an allowlist of 3,195 of 3,849. The STATUS problem is NOT, and no filter could fix it - all 3,195 ship at CONFIDENCE_LOW because `featuresta` says Active about every one of them. THE ORIGINAL REFUSAL, unchanged: UNSUITABLE, and it is a refusal rather than a gap - the second in this survey and a different shape from DEC's. 'NYC Parks Drinking Fountains' (qnv7-p7a2) is 3,849 real rows attributed to NYC Parks, so the data exists; what is missing is any way to tell which of them a hiker can drink from. Measured live 2026-09-15: (1) `featuresta` reads 'Active' on ALL 3,849 rows - zero variance, so a status column that looks like it says something and does not, which is worse than no column because a reader assumes it means something, and NYC Parks shuts fountains off over winter; (2) `fountainty` mixes 292 'Indoor Drinking Fountain' and 120 'Food Prep Sink' in with the outdoor ones, and the rest are letters - A 981, C 630, E 385, D 377, B 140 - plus 118 'Bottle Filler High Low'; those letters were undecoded when this verdict was taken and are not any more (#1461: PIP's element names spell A-F out as drinking fountains), so the allowlist blocker is gone and the status blocker is what remains; (3) rowsUpdatedAt 2024-07-15, fourteen months stale against the trails layer's monthly automation. Together those mean a pin from this layer would assert 'there is working drinking water here' on the strength of a column saying Active about a food-prep sink capped in 2024. See nyc_water_holdback. DEC's refusal was about what the data IS; this one is about what it does not SAY.

dec_water_holdback: WHY NO WATER SHIPS FROM DEC, recorded beside the sources rather than only in a survey, because the next person to look at dec_backcountry_features will see 'SPRING' and 'WELL' in its ASSET column and reasonably wonder (#1097; the evidence is POI_COVERAGE_SURVEY.md §3, the verdict is poi_coverage.orgs['NYS DEC'].types.water, and tests/test_poi_coverage.py pins it). Measured live 2026-08-27: DEC's only plumbed-water asset type is 'WATER SUPPLY SYSTEM', 23 features, and ZERO of them are flagged PUBLICUSE 'Y' - DEC's own answer is that none of it is for visitors. Sampling 14 found real spigots beside a 'Water Storage Tank', an 'Underground Water Line', and a drilled well whose own NOTES read 'Not Approved For Human Consum[ption]'. The 350 features whose names merely SOUND like water are worse and are also all PUBLICUSE 'N': 207 'WATERHOLE' are fire-and-wildlife impoundments ('Wetland Pool', 'Made by Tioga County SWCD in 2016'), 97 'WELL' are dominated by NATURAL GAS WELLS, 4 'CISTERN' are CCC-era fire cisterns, and 19 'SPRING' include one 'Unnoffical Unsanctioned Traditional Public Wa[ter]' and one 'Untested'. A pipeline matching on the word 'water' would have published 207 fire ponds and 97 gas wells as places to fill a bottle. The maintainer's decision on reading this, 2026-08-27: 'Lets not use water from DEC'. Reopening it should mean NEW DATA FROM DEC - a layer they publish, a flag that flips - and never a new reading of these same 23 rows.

nyc_water_holdback._comment: WHY NEW YORK CITY'S DRINKING FOUNTAINS WERE HELD, AND WHAT CHANGED (#1452, then #1461). THEY SHIP NOW - 3,195 of the 3,849, every one at CONFIDENCE_LOW - and this block is kept because only ONE of the two blockers below was ever answered. Read it as the standing reason the OTHER one is carried by `confidence_floor` on nyc_drinking_fountains rather than as a refusal still in force. The original title was `why they do not ship`. Placed between dec_water_holdback and oprhp_water_holdback deliberately: all three are measured decisions about a water source rather than omissions, and a reader comparing them sees three different ways the question resolves. DEC'S WAS ABOUT WHAT THE DATA IS - 23 'WATER SUPPLY SYSTEM' features, none flagged for public use. OPRHP'S WAS A YES that raised the evidence bar. THIS ONE IS ABOUT WHAT THE DATA DOES NOT SAY. 'NYC Parks Drinking Fountains' (qnv7-p7a2) carries 3,849 rows and they are real; measured live 2026-09-15, what it does not carry is any way to tell a working outdoor fountain from a capped one or from a kitchen sink. `featuresta` reads 'Active' on every single row - a status column with zero variance, which is worse than an absent one because it reads as an answer, and NYC Parks shuts fountains off over winter. `fountainty` holds 292 'Indoor Drinking Fountain' and 120 'Food Prep Sink' among the rest, whose values are undecoded letters (A 981, C 630, E 385, D 377, B 140) plus 118 'Bottle Filler High Low'. And rowsUpdatedAt is 2024-07-15, fourteen months stale against the trails layer's monthly automation. Any one would be survivable; together they mean a pin would assert 'there is working drinking water here' on the strength of a column saying Active about a sink somebody capped in 2024. CHASED 2026-09-15 (#1461), AND HALF OF IT CAME BACK. The dataset's own Data Dictionary link, which it publishes in its description, is DEAD - Google Drive answers 404, so the domain is not merely unpublished beside the column, the document NYC Parks points readers at is gone. But the letters decode from a sibling: 'Parks Inspection Program - Element Tracking' (2jvr-j6ne) spells the same vocabulary out as elements - 'A' Drinking Fountain 28,577 rows, 'C' 17,301, 'E' 13,611, 'D' 11,670, 'B' 5,080, 'F' 1,953. So A through F ARE drinking fountains in NYC Parks' own inspection language, 2,536 of the 2,563 lettered rows, and only G (7), H (12) and J (8) remain unplaced. AN OUTDOOR-DRINKING ALLOWLIST IS THEREFORE CONSTRUCTIBLE, which it was not when this block was written - an inference from the two vocabularies matching rather than from NYC Parks saying so, and to be labelled that way wherever it is used. WHAT STILL BLOCKS IT IS THE OTHER HALF, and re-measuring did not move it: featuresta is still 'Active' on all 3,849. The PIP series carries condition and it JOINS - 'Parks Inspection Program - Inspections' (yg3y-7juh) keys prop_id in the same borough-letter convention as gispropnum, and inspection_id reaches element rows carrying damaged, outstanding, free-text comments and nowatercount ('number of water features without water'). Measured: 876 of the 988 park properties holding fountains have been inspected (88.7%), 2,334 of 3,849 fountains sit on an ever-inspected property (60.6%), and 2,064 (53.6%) on one inspected in 2026, most recent inspection 2026-06-30. THREE LIMITS DECIDE WHAT MAY BE SAID FROM IT: it is PROPERTY-level, never fountain-level; it is NEGATIVE-ONLY, because across 97,596 drinking-fountain element rows nowatercount is populated 1,182 times and reads 0 exactly three times, so null means not-recorded and there is no positive evidence of a working fountain anywhere in it; and it covers just over half. So what became available is a dated park-level warning - this park was inspected on D and n of its fountains had no water - and NOT a claim that any fountain works. Shipping that is a decision about a card on a safety path and is the maintainer's; this block records that the question was chased and where it got to, not a new verdict. THE MECHANICAL GUARD HAS MOVED, and saying so is the point of this sentence surviving. It used to be that no NYC layer was registered as a POI source at all, so nothing could draw these by accident. That is no longer true: nyc_drinking_fountains is registered and exporting. What guards the remaining blocker now is `confidence_floor` on that entry, which forces every row to CONFIDENCE_LOW, and the allowlist `where` that keeps the sinks and the undecoded letters out. Both are enforcement rather than record, and both are one careless edit from being undone - which is why they carry their own comments there.
nyc_water_holdback.open_question: https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/1461 - the `fountainty` domain question is ANSWERED (A-F decode against PIP element names, see _comment), and what is left is narrower and is the maintainer's: whether a park-level, negative-only, half-covering inspection signal is worth drawing at all, and in what shape. #1452 is where the original refusal was measured.

oprhp_water_holdback: WHY OPRHP'S WATER DOES NOT SHIP EITHER, and why its reason is different from DEC's (#1097). OPRHP's water is REAL: 136 'Water Spigot' and 15 'Drinking Fountain' in NY_State_Park_Facilities' Sub_Asset, measured live 2026-08-27, plumbed fixtures named as such - so unlike DEC this is a holdback rather than a refusal, and the poi_coverage verdict stays `available` rather than `unsuitable`. Two things have to be answered first, and neither is answerable from the layer. (1) SEASONALITY IS UNRECORDED. A park spigot is shut off for winter and the layer carries no field saying when; a pin promising water in April where the valve is closed is the failure FEATURES.md names - a confidently wrong prediction is more dangerous than an honest unknown - and water is one of CLAUDE.md's four ways this app can hurt somebody. (2) OPRHP'S OWN APP SHOWS ONLY 15 OF THE 151: every Water Spigot reads ParksApp 'N', so the org itself puts only the drinking fountains in front of visitors, and publishing the other 136 would be going further than the steward does with their own data. Everything else OPRHP publishes ships (shelter, campsite, privy, viewpoint, parking, crossing); this one type waits for an issue of its own with its own evidence, which is the shape export_poi.py's osm_water treatment already sets. Also NOT water and never to be folded in: 'Mineral Spring' (17), 'Water Tower' (12), 'Waterfall' (55).

usfs_licence._comment: The basis on which usfs_trails and usfs_rec_sites may be fetched AND republished to hikers: PUBLIC DOMAIN under 17 U.S.C. 105, adopted by the maintainer on 2026-09-02 ("Move the usfs licence to the public domain"). THIS BLOCK RECORDS A READING OF A STATUTE, NOT A GRANT FROM AN AGENCY, and the difference is the whole reason it is written at length. Section 105 says copyright protection is not available for any work of the United States Government - a work prepared by an officer or employee as part of their official duties. The TrailNFS publish layer and the INFRA recreation-site layer are exactly that, so there is no copyright for the Forest Service to license, withhold, or condition. That is why the licence_basis is `stated_by_org` rather than `maintainer_authorisation`: licence_basis_comment's own vocabulary names 'a federal public-domain work' as an instance of terms that permit this use, and unlike DEC or NYNJTC there is no unanswered ask sitting behind it. THE PATH THIS TOOK, recorded because the file moved twice in one day and a reader deserves to see why rather than a final state that looks obvious. It registered `unresolved` on the morning of 2026-09-02 - the Forest Service states no terms anywhere this survey could read, and the survey declined to settle the statute on their behalf. The maintainer then authorised publication on the grounds that the data is publicly available, which was recorded as `maintainer_authorisation` because public availability is not itself a reuse grant (SOURCE_SURVEY.md's rule, and the rule under which DEC, NYNJTC and Mohonk all sit in that column). The maintainer then made the stronger and more accurate call, which is this one. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY READ FROM THE SERVICES, unchanged by any of that and still worth having: copyrightText is EMPTY at the service level on EDW_TrailNFSPublish_01, read live 2026-09-02; the LAYER carries the bare string 'USDA Forest Service', which is an attribution rather than a grant; EDW_RecreationOpportunities_01 carries a no-warranty disclaimer, which is a disclaimer rather than a grant. Neither service is an AGOL item - both are on-prem ArcGIS - so there is no licenseInfo to quote the way nynjtc_licence and mohonk_licence quote one. NONE OF THAT IS EVIDENCE AGAINST SECTION 105; silence from an agency is what the statute predicts, because there is nothing for them to say. THE LIMITS, which are real and are not licence questions. (1) Section 105 is DOMESTIC: it removes U.S. copyright, and other jurisdictions are not bound by it. (2) It covers works of GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES; a federal agency can hold copyright assigned to it by a contractor, and nothing here has audited these two layers for contributed third-party content. (3) It is not a warranty of accuracy, and the Forest Service's own disclaimer stands - which matters more for a hiker than the licence does. (4) Public domain is not a trademark licence: the Forest Service shield is a mark, is protected separately (18 U.S.C. 711a), and org_marks still reads `not_asked` for USFS. What ships is the DATA. ATTRIBUTION IS KEPT ANYWAY, and is not owed: `attribution` stays 'USDA Forest Service' on both entries because telling a hiker whose survey a line came from is this project's practice regardless of whether a licence compels it.
usfs_licence.author: USDA Forest Service
usfs_licence.author_note: Spelled to match usfs_trails' and usfs_rec_sites' `steward` verbatim, which is what export_sources.py joins on - the failure usdm_licence's own author_note records, where an author matching no steward meant the recorded terms silently never reached the sources screen. That test caught this entry twice in one day: once at registration, and again when the nationwide rename changed the steward and this field did not follow.
usfs_licence.license: Public domain (work of the U.S. Government, 17 U.S.C. 105)
usfs_licence.basis: 17 U.S.C. 105, adopted by the maintainer 2026-09-02 ("Move the usfs licence to the public domain")
usfs_licence.open_question: None that blocks anything, which makes this the only source family in the registry with no licence ask outstanding - the Forest Service has nothing to answer. What remains is narrower and is listed in _comment: the statute is domestic, it does not reach contractor-held copyright if any of this layer contains contributed content, and it says nothing about the Forest Service's shield, which stays unasked in org_marks. https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/1207 is where this was decided.

njdep_licence._comment: The basis on which the two New Jersey layers above (njdep_park_trails, nj_statewide_trails) may be fetched, and the bar their data has to clear before any of it is republished to hikers. TERMS ARE STATED, for the first time on a trail-line source in this registry beyond OPRHP's: the Forum item carries the NJDEP Data Distribution Agreement as its licenseInfo, 1,968 characters, read WHOLE on 2026-09-09 (the survey's own instruction, in bold, for the oprhp_licence reason - a licence once misread through a 200-character truncation) and quoted verbatim below. WHAT IT SAYS, condition by condition. It is a distribution agreement, so it PERMITS reproduction and redistribution - conditions 1 and 2 speak of 'any reproduction or manipulation' and of data 'reproduced or redistributed', which are acts it regulates rather than forbids. It DISCLAIMS everything: as-is, no warranty of any kind, no duty to maintain or update, no warranty that the data is free of third-party copyright or trademark claims (condition 4), and the user is 'responsible for understanding the accuracy limitations' documented in the cross-reference files. It REQUIRES three things: (1) that 'the coordinate reference system remains intact' in any reproduction - satisfied by construction if the published lines stay in the CRS the layer serves them in (WGS84 through the export; the reprojection export_trails.py does to simplify in metres is a manipulation whose OUTPUT is back in WGS84, and whether that is 'intact' is a reading nobody has taken); (2) that the data 'may not be reproduced or redistributed without all the metadata provided' - the item description, this agreement, and the cross-reference the agreement itself refers to, which means the Sources screen (export_sources.py) would have to carry NJDEP's metadata wholesale rather than a name and a licence line, a surface this project does not have; (3) that 'any maps, publications, reports, or other documents' using the data credit NJDEP's GIS 'with the following credit/disclaimer' - the sentence in attribution_required, verbatim, which map/credits.ts would have to print in those words and not in a paraphrase. NONE OF THESE IS A REFUSAL, AND NONE IS SATISFIED TODAY, which is why licence_basis reads `unresolved` on both entries and reaches_hikers false: satisfying (2) and (3) is a deliberate act with a design question inside it (where a hiker reads a paragraph of NJDEP's metadata), and the maintainer decides whether that act is worth New Jersey's lines. When it is taken and recorded here, the basis becomes `stated_by_org` - the terms are NJDEP's own and they permit this - on the same footing as oprhp_licence. WHERE THE AGREEMENT IS AND IS NOT STATED. It is stated on the Forum item only. NJDEP's on-prem service (mapsdep.nj.gov) carries copyrightText 'NJDEP' at the service and layer level and no terms text at all, read live 2026-09-09. Both are owned by the same NJDEPBGIS account, so the agreement is read as governing the park layer too - an inference from the owner and not from anything that layer says, and recorded as one.
njdep_licence.author: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection
njdep_licence.license: NJDEP Data Distribution Agreement: reuse and redistribution permitted as-is, on condition of the coordinate reference system kept intact, the metadata redistributed with the data, and NJDEP's credit/disclaimer sentence verbatim on any map - all three satisfied since 2026-09-11, see basis
njdep_licence.terms_verbatim: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP) Data Distribution Agreement. The data provided herein are distributed subject to the following conditions and restrictions: NJDEP assumes no responsibility to maintain them in any manner or form and disclaims any duty or obligation to either maintain availability of or to update the data. Terms of Agreement 1. All data is provided, as is, without any representation or warranty of any kind, implied, expressed or statutory including, but not limited to, the warranties of non-infringement of third party rights, title, merchantability or fitness for a particular use, freedom from computer virus nor are any such warranties to be implied with respect to the digital data layers furnished hereunder. User is responsible for understanding the accuracy limitations of all digital data layers provided herein, as documented in the accompanying cross-reference files (see SUPPLEMENTAL INFORMATION). Any reproduction or manipulation of the above data must ensure that the coordinate reference system remains intact. 2. njdep_licence.terms_source: https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=2fa0ddfecdf74f8a8718bd3791dabdd7 (licenseInfo field, 1,968 characters, read in full 2026-09-09); https://mapsdep.nj.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Features/Land/MapServer/63?f=json carries copyrightText 'NJDEP' and no terms, read the same day
njdep_licence.attribution_required: This (map/publication/report) was developed using New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection Geographic Information System digital data, but this secondary product has not been verified by NJDEP and is not state-authorized or endorsed.
njdep_licence.basis: RESOLVED 2026-09-11 on the maintainer's decision, recorded here because a determination nobody can inspect is worth no more than an assertion. The terms are NJDEP's own, read whole and quoted verbatim above, and they permit reuse and redistribution; what was missing was the decision to satisfy the two conditions that needed building, and that decision is taken. WHAT WAS BUILT TO MEET THEM. Condition 1, the coordinate reference system intact: satisfied by construction - the published lines are WGS84, which is the CRS the layers serve, and export_trails.py's reprojection to metres is an intermediate whose output returns to WGS84. Condition 3, the credit/disclaimer verbatim on any map: `attribution` on both entries is now `attribution_required` below, byte for byte, so the sentence NJDEP requires is the sentence chrome/SourcesSection.tsx prints - that component renders licence and attribution verbatim on purpose ('A licence is a condition somebody agreed to and an attribution is what it obliges; neither is this app's wording to adjust'). Condition 2, the metadata redistributed with the data: export_sources.py now publishes this block's `terms_verbatim` and `terms_source` on the steward record, so the agreement travels with the lines and the item it came from is one link away, rather than a name and a one-line summary. WHAT IS STILL HONESTLY OPEN, said rather than closed over. 'All the metadata provided' is NJDEP's phrase and it plausibly means more than the agreement and the item URL - the cross-reference files condition 1 names are not republished here, and a stricter reading wants them. This is the maintainer's reading recorded as such, not NJDEP's confirmation; NJDEP has not been asked. A club that inherits this project re-reads the agreement in its own name. The remedy if the reading is wrong is one field per source and a re-run, which is the whole reason the gate is a registry field rather than a code path.
njdep_licence.open_question: https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/1293 - the maintainer's decision on conditions 2 and 3, and where a hiker reads NJDEP's metadata; and, once the layers ship, whether the 166 managing agencies behind the statewide compilation want naming beyond NJDEP's own credit.

nyc_licence._comment: The basis on which nyc_parks_trails and nyc_dot_greenways above may be fetched AND republished to hikers, and it is the FIRST STATUTORY GRANT IN THIS REGISTRY. Every other non-ATC source here is unstated (dec_licence, nynjtc_licence, mohonk_licence), conditioned (njdep_licence) or restricted (oprhp_licence's non-commercial clause, which is still an open ask). New York City's is none of those. NYC Local Law 11 of 2012, codified at Administrative Code 23-502(d), requires that a published data set be available 'without registration requirement, license requirement, or usage restrictions'. That is a grant made BY STATUTE TO EVERYONE rather than a permission granted to this project - which is why it needs no ask, cannot be withdrawn by an agency changing its mind about a portal field, and does not have to be re-confirmed in its own name by a club that inherits this project. WHERE IT IS NOT READ FROM, said because this file has been wrong about a licence once before by reading the wrong field: not from the dataset pages, which carry no licence at all - `license` is null and `licenseId` absent on both vjbm-hsyr and mzxg-pwib, verified live 2026-09-15. Their silence here means the statute applies, and is the opposite of what the same silence means on DEC's or Mohonk's services, where nothing stands behind it. The City's own published standards are what quote the law and add the two riders below.
nyc_licence.author: New York City Department of Parks and Recreation
also_covers: New York City Department of Transportation
nyc_licence.also_covers_comment: One city, two agencies, one statute - recorded as a single block rather than two because the terms are not the agencies' to set and are identical by law. THIS FIELD IS READ, and saying so matters: export_sources.py matches a block to a steward on `author`, and NYC DOT is not this block's author, so before `also_covers` was a list the exporter honoured, NYC DOT shipped to hikers with `licence: null` while this block sat in the registry looking correct. That is the exact failure usdm_licence's `author_note` records - 'the block sits in the registry looking correct, the exporter emits null, the card renders attribution alone, and every test passes' - and prose here naming the other agency did nothing to stop it. tests/test_export_sources.py pins both stewards' licence text now.
nyc_licence.license: NYC Local Law 11 of 2012, Administrative Code 23-502(d) - published data sets are available without registration requirement, license requirement, or usage restrictions
nyc_licence.terms_verbatim: data sets must be available without registration requirement, license requirement, or usage restrictions, except as provided below
nyc_licence.terms_source: NYC Open Data Technical Standards Manual, 'Public policies' (https://cityofnewyork.github.io/opendatatsm/publicpolicies.html), the City's own published standards, which quote Local Law 11 of 2012 and state the reuse conditions below; read 2026-09-15. The statute itself is NYC Administrative Code 23-502(d) and 23-504. Both dataset pages carry no licence field of their own, read live the same day.
nyc_licence.attribution_required: A CONDITION, and a wider one than any other block here asks for. The City's standards say DoITT (now OTI) may require a third party republishing a data set to 'explicitly identify the source, version, and modifications made to a public data set'. SOURCE IS SATISFIED - client/src/map/credits.ts's NYC_PARKS_CREDIT and NYC_DOT_CREDIT put both agencies in the map corner whenever their lines are drawn, and export_sources.py carries them to the Sources screen. VERSION AND MODIFICATIONS ARE NOT, and that is written here rather than left for somebody to find: this app has no surface on which a hiker reads which vintage of a steward's layer they are looking at, and nyc_dot_greenways ships MODIFIED in a way a reader cannot see from the map, filtered to 3,039 of 29,695 rows. njdep_licence records the same shape of gap for New Jersey. THE REASON THIS ONE SHIPS AND THAT ONE DID NOT is the difference between the two texts, not a change of posture: NJDEP's agreement says data 'may not be reproduced or redistributed without all the metadata provided', which is a precondition on the act, where the City's standards say OTI 'may require' identification, which is a reservation of a power nobody has exercised. @unvalidated - nobody has asked OTI whether they require it for a map of this kind, and asking is what would settle it. If the answer is yes, the fix is the stewards artifact (lib/stewards.ts), which already lists exactly the sources a release ships and is where a version and a filter note belong.
nyc_licence.warranty: None, and stated plainly: 'The City does not warranty the completeness, accuracy, content, or fitness for any particular purpose or use of any public data set', and the City is 'not liable for any deficiencies' in the same. That is boilerplate everywhere except on the paths CLAUDE.md's 'Four ways this app can hurt somebody' names, and it is relevant on one of them here: nyc_parks_trails carries segments last surveyed in 2013, and the City is explicit that it does not stand behind their accuracy.
nyc_licence.basis: The statute is the basis, and the maintainer's authorisation of 2026-09-15 sits beside it for the attribution rider only. Recorded as two things rather than one because they answer different questions: the right to fetch, republish and draw these lines comes from Local Law 11 and would exist if nobody here had decided anything, while the decision to ship before the version-and-modifications identification is built is a judgement the maintainer made, on the reading in attribution_required above. If that reading is wrong, what is wrong is the shape of the credit and not the right to draw the lines.
nyc_licence.open_question: https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/1432 - whether OTI requires the version-and-modifications identification for a map of this kind, and where a hiker would read it. Also open, and smaller: the 2,095 greenway segments whose jurisdiction is NYC Parks rather than DOT are covered by both registered layers, and whether the same tread is drawn twice has not been measured.

usfs_dispersed_camping_holdback._comment: WHY USFS's LARGEST SITE TYPE DOES NOT SHIP (#1207). 'CAMPING AREA' is 10,783 of usfs_rec_sites' 31,405 rows - bigger than CAMPGROUND (4,183) and GROUP CAMPGROUND (422) combined, and the single largest type in the layer. It is DISPERSED CAMPING, and this project has already decided not to publish that. THE EVIDENCE THAT IT IS DISPERSED, measured live 2026-09-02, because the type name alone does not say so. (1) development_scale reads 0 - undeveloped - on 8,135 of the 10,783, with 1,549 at scale 1 and 1,099 at scale 2. CAMPGROUND is the opposite shape: 3 on 2,490 rows, 4 on 960, 5 on 139, 2 on 594, and NOT ONE at 0 or 1. The two types do not overlap on the development scale at all. (2) The names are road references rather than places - 'FS1302-03', 'RD 614 SITE 13', 'RD 201 MI 8.2', 'LCR 839C-001', 'BRD21405-001', 'EAST FORK RESERVOIR RD-002' - which is what a catalogue of individual pull-offs along a forest road looks like, not a campground directory. THE DECISION THIS FOLLOWS IS NOT NEW. SOURCE_SURVEY.md section 3b holds back ATC's Campsite Sustainability Index for the same reason - 2,333 user-created campsites, 'publishing locations may be actively harmful', the ones land managers are often trying to close - and .claude/skills/pr-screenshot/SKILL.md names 'a dispersed or user-created campsite at a readable zoom' as one of four things that must never appear even in a SCREENSHOT, on the grounds that a map is a publication of coordinates. Shipping 10,783 of them as poi_type campsite would be that same publication at 4.6x the scale of the holdback that set the precedent, and it would arrive as a side effect of a change about the White Mountains rather than as a decision anybody took. WHAT WOULD REOPEN IT: the maintainer deciding that the Forest Service publishing these itself changes the argument - which is a real position, and different from ATC's case in that USFS is the land manager rather than a third party cataloguing what hikers made. That is a decision with an issue of its own, not a line in this one. THE MECHANICAL GUARD is export_nearby_poi.py's USFS_SITE_TYPES allowlist, which maps four types and no others.
